'''Blake Michael''' (born July 31, 1996) is an American former actor, businessman, and journalist. He played Charlie Delgado in the [[Disney Channel]] original movie ''[[Lemonade Mouth (film)|Lemonade Mouth]]'' (2011) and Tyler James in the Disney Channel series ''[[Dog with a Blog]]'' (2012–2015), which won him the [[Young Artist Award]] for [[34th Young Artist Awards#Best Performance in a TV Series - Leading Young Actor|Best Leading Young Actor in a Television Series]]. For directing the [[short film]] ''Notes of Hers'' (2013), he won the Audience Choice Award from the [[Red Rock Film Festival]].

{{As of|2025|}}, his last role was in a 2019 episode of ''[[What Just Happened??! with Fred Savage]]'', choosing to focus on other endeavors. In 2021, Michael became the Chief Evangelist of Lumanu, a [[Online presence management|social media management]] company aimed at helping online creators manage their brand and business, and began writing for ''[[Forbes]]'' as a marketing expert and business analyst.

==Life and career==
Michael was born in [[Atlanta]], [[Georgia (U.S. state)|Georgia]], and is of [[Puerto Rico|Puerto Rican]] and [[History of the Jews in Russia|Russian Jewish]] descent.<ref>{{Cite tweet|number=429274546085310465|user=BlakeMichael14|title=I'm part Russian (|author=Blake Michael}}</ref> Michael's career as a [[child actor]] began at the age of three, when he started booking print ad jobs. Michael enrolled at the Company Acting Studio in Atlanta at the age of five, and was discovered by a talent agent when he was six.<ref name=":1">{{Cite journal |date=October 30, 2013 |title=7th Annual RED ROCK FILM FESTIVAL GUIDE |url=https://issuu.com/redrockfilmfestival/docs/rrff_guide-2013-w |journal=[[Red Rock Film Festival|Red Rock Film Festival Guide]] |pages=20–21 |via=[[Issuu]]}}</ref> His first commercial role was for [[Bojangles (restaurant)|Bojangles' Famous Chicken]], alongside [[National Football League|NFL]] quarterback [[Jake Delhomme]]. At age ten, he was chosen to host of a series of four commercials for [[Hasbro|Hasbro Toys]] that would air on [[Cartoon Network]]. After the ad campaign, Cartoon Network invited Michael to present and host his own show on the network, which culminated in two shows named ''Fried Dynamite'', which aired on Fridays, and ''Dynamite Action Squad!'' on Saturdays.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Bio – Blake Michael |url=https://www.blakemichael.com/bio1 |access-date=May 16, 2022 |website=Blake Michael Official Website}}</ref>

In May 2010, Blake appeared in ''[[No Limit Kids: Much Ado About Middle School]]'' and later joined with the film's star, country singer Celeste Kellogg, to create and sing a duet titled "Looking In Your Eyes".<ref>{{Cite AV media |url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=KulVxS5v-bM |title=CELESTE KELLOGG "Looking in Your Eyes" Official Vid with BLAKE MICHAEL! |date=January 31, 2011 |type=Music video}}</ref> He made a small cameo in Kellogg's music video "My Jeans".<ref>{{Cite AV media |url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=3l9UqMnBPYQ |title=Celeste Kellogg - My Jeans (Official Music Video) |date=September 18, 2009 |type=Music video}}</ref> In June 2010, he was discovered in an open casting call and was cast in a co-lead role as Charlie Delgado in the [[Disney Channel]] made-for-TV movie musical ''[[Lemonade Mouth (film)|Lemonade Mouth]]''.<ref name="casting">{{cite web |last=Andreeva |first=Nellie |date=August 4, 2010 |title=Disney Channel Casts Its Next Big Musical |url=https://deadline.com/2010/08/disney-channel-casts-its-next-big-musical-59499/ |access-date=May 5, 2016 |website=[[Deadline Hollywood]] }}</ref> Michael later called this role the one that "catapulted his career" and "helped him gain an audience".<ref>{{Cite web |last=Michael |first=Blake |date=March 28, 2022 |title=Creators: How To Turn Your Online Presence Into A Real-World Business |url=https://www.forbes.com/sites/forbesbusinesscouncil/2022/03/28/creators-how-to-turn-your-online-presence-into-a-real-world-business/ |access-date=May 8, 2022 |website=[[Forbes]]}}</ref> Soon after, Disney approached Michael and asked him to read for a role on an upcoming sitcom.<ref>{{Cite Instagram|postid=CU7pcDnFxBX|user=blakemichael14|title=Out of the blue Disney came to me and had me read for what was then a show with a title I almost turned down. "Dog with a Blog"|date=October 12, 2021|author=Blake Michael}}</ref> Michael later accepted the role as Tyler James in the Disney Channel sitcom ''[[Dog with a Blog]]'', who he portrayed from 2012 to 2015.<ref name=":4">{{cite news |author=Jethro Nededog |date=April 13, 2012 |title=Disney Channel Announces Series Pickup for 'Dog With a Blog' |work=[[The Hollywood Reporter]] |url=https://www.hollywoodreporter.com/live-feed/dog-with-a-blog-disney-channel-series-pickup-311998 |accessdate=May 5, 2016}}</ref>

As a director, Michael directed the short film ''Anonymous'' in 2011, and ''Notes of Hers'' in 2013, the latter of which was featured at the Toronto Student Film Festival, and won the Audience Choice Award at the [[Red Rock Film Festival]].<ref name=":0" /><ref name=":1" /> In 2015, he appeared as Chase in the [[Lifetime (TV network)|Lifetime]] [[Television film|television movie]] ''I Killed My BFF''.<ref name=":5">{{cite web |title=I Killed My BFF |url=http://www.mylifetime.com/movies/i-killed-my-bff-the-movie |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150612025820/http://www.mylifetime.com/movies/i-killed-my-bff-the-movie |archive-date=June 12, 2015 |access-date=May 5, 2016 |publisher=[[Lifetime (TV network)|Lifetime]] }}</ref> In 2018, he voiced Curtis in eight episodes of ''[[Voltron: Legendary Defender]].''<ref name=":6">{{Cite web |title=Voltron: Legendary Defender (2016) |url=https://www.behindthevoiceactors.com/tv-shows/Voltron-Legendary-Defender/ |access-date=May 8, 2022 |website=Behind the Voice Actors}}</ref> In 2019, he was featured as Pete in ''[[Princess of the Row]]'', which premiered at the [[Cinequest Film & Creativity Festival|Cinequest Film Festival]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=Emerson |first=Andrew |date=March 23, 2019 |title=Princess of the Row |url=https://filmthreat.com/reviews/princess-of-the-row/ |access-date=May 8, 2022 |website=[[Film Threat]]}}</ref>

In 2021, Michael joined the board of directors of Lumanu, a social media management company, as the Chief Evangelist.<ref name=":2">{{Cite web |title=Lumanu {{!}} About Us |url=https://www.lumanu.com/about |access-date=May 8, 2022 |website=Lumanu}}</ref> He was inspired to help other creators elevate their social status on the internet instead of following what he called the "traditional Hollywood film route", using experience he gained from becoming one of the first and youngest people to be officially [[YouTube Partner|partnered with YouTube]] from a young age.<ref>{{Cite podcast |url=https://podcasts.apple.com/us/podcast/blake-michael-the-future-of-how-companies/id1493357557?i=1000555827785 |title=Blake Michael: The future of how companies work with creators |website=Creators Are Brands |publisher=[[Apple Podcasts]] |host=Tom Boyd |date=March 31, 2022 |access-date=May 25, 2022}}</ref> He also began writing for ''Forbes'' as a marketing expert, and to promote Lumanu's services, that same year.<ref name=":3">{{Cite web |title=Blake Michael - Forbes Councils |url=https://profiles.forbes.com/members/business/profile/Blake-Michael-Chief-Evangelist-Officer-Lumanu/903ccb78-55eb-41ba-a0b7-3cd99c1f8f3d |access-date=May 8, 2022 |website=[[Forbes]]}}</ref>

==Personal life==
Michael married longtime girlfriend, Ariel Mullen, in Italy on October 10, 2024.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Former Disney Star Blake Michael Unveils Wedding Photos After Quietly Getting Married to Ariel Mullen Last Year |url=https://people.com/disney-blake-michael-marries-ariel-mullen-wedding-photos-11739172 |access-date=2025-05-24 |website=People.com |language=en}}</ref>

{{Short description|American football player and professional wrestler (born 1991)}} {{Use American English|date=October 2025}} {{Use mdy dates|date=October 2025}} {{Infobox person | image = Mason Madden (cropped).jpg | image_size = | alt = | caption = Williams in August 2025 | birth_name = Brennan Marcel Williams | birth_date = {{Birth date and age|1991|2|5|mf=y}} | birth_place = [[Easton, Massachusetts|Easton]], [[Massachusetts]], U.S. | education = [[University of North Carolina at Chapel Hill|UNC Chapel Hill]] | spouse = Ciarra Williams | children = 3 | family = [[Brent Williams (American football)|Brent Williams]] (father) | module = {{Infobox professional wrestler | child = yes | ring_names = {{ubl|Brennan Williams|Dio Maddin|Mace|ma.çé|Marcellus Black|Mase Madden{{cite news |last1=Lafferriere |first1=Nicolas|date=December 11, 2023 |title=Mace y Mansoor realizan su primera aparición fuera de WWE |url=https://solowrestling.mundodeportivo.com/new/125833-wwe-mace-mansoor-aparicion-en-dpw |work=Solo Wrestling |language=es |access-date=December 11, 2023}}|'''Mason Madden'''{{cite web |last=Carey |first=Ian |date=January 17, 2024 |title=Mace: Fox nixed plans for WWE Retribution angle |url=https://www.f4wonline.com/news/wwe/mace-fox-nixed-plans-for-wwe-retribution-angle |access-date=March 9, 2024 |website=[[Wrestling Observer]]}}|Mason D. Madden}} | height = 6 ft 8 in{{cite web|url=https://www.wwe.com/superstars/mace|title=ma.çé WWE|website=WWE.com}} | weight = 286 lb{{cite web|url= https://www.cagematch.net/?id=2&nr=17990|title=ma.ce « Wrestlers Database « CAGEMATCH - The Internet Wrestling Database|website=Cagematch.net}} | billed = "The savage lands of [[Shaolin Monastery|Shaolin]]"{{cite web |url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=CjipnylI3oE |title=Marcellus Black Wrestling Debut: The Shogun of the Row |publisher=Title Match Wrestling |via=YouTube |date=February 10, 2016 |access-date=July 25, 2016 |quote=See between 1:49 to 1:55}} | trainer = {{ubl|[[Booker T (wrestler)|Booker T]]|[[Reality of Wrestling]]}} | debut = February 1, 2016 | retired = | website = }} | module2 = {{Infobox gridiron football biography | embed = yes | name = Brennan Williams | image = | image_size = | alt = | caption = | number = 73, 65 | position = [[Offensive tackle]] | height_ft = 6 | height_in = 6 | weight_lbs = 314 | high_school = [[Catholic Memorial School|Catholic Memorial]]
([[West Roxbury, Massachusetts]]) | college = [[North Carolina Tar Heels football|North Carolina]] | draftyear = 2013 | draftround = 3 | draftpick = 89 | pastteams = * [[Houston Texans]] ({{NFL Year|2013}}) * [[Jacksonville Jaguars]] ({{NFL Year|2015}})* * [[New England Patriots]] ({{NFL Year|2015}})* | highlights = | pfr = W/WillBr03 }} }} '''Brennan Marcel Williams'''{{cite web|title=NFL's Brennan Williams Now Wrestling as "Marcellus Black"| date=December 14, 2015 |url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=TGaiVWV3cck|access-date=July 20, 2016|publisher=Title Match Wrestling}} (born February 5, 1991) is an American [[professional wrestler]] and former [[American football|football]] player. He is signed to [[All Elite Wrestling]] (AEW) and its sister promotion [[Ring of Honor]] (ROH), where he performs under the [[ring name]] '''Mason Madden''' and is a member of MxM TV and its sub-group [[MxM Collection]] alongside [[Mansoor (wrestler)|Mansoor]]. He also makes appearances on the [[independent circuit]]. He is best known for his tenure in [[WWE]], where he performed under the ring names '''Dio Maddin''', '''Mace''', and '''ma.çé'''. Prior to beginning his professional wrestling career, Williams played [[college football]] for the [[North Carolina Tar Heels football|North Carolina Tar Heels]]. He was selected by the [[Houston Texans]] of the [[National Football League]] (NFL) in the third round of the [[2013 NFL draft]]. He joined [[WWE]] from 2016 to 2023. ==Early life== Williams was born in [[North Easton, Massachusetts]], and attended [[Catholic Memorial School]] in the [[West Roxbury]] neighborhood of [[Boston]]. While at Catholic Memorial, Williams was a member of ''[[PrepStar College Recruiting|PrepStar]]''{{'}}s High School All-America team, a member of the "Super 26" team in 2008, an all-scholastic by the ''[[Boston Globe]]'' and ''[[Boston Herald]]''. He was named all-conference as both a junior and senior. He was rated as the eighth best offensive lineman in the country by SuperPrep All-America. [[Rivals.com]] rated him the seventh best offensive guard in the country. [[Scout.com]] rated him as the 15th best offensive lineman in the country. [[ESPN.com]] rated him the 35th best offensive tackle in the country. He was also a member of the Rivals 250. He also played in the [[U.S. Army All-American Bowl]]. On February 15, 2014, Williams's number 73 was retired by Catholic Memorial.{{cite web |url=https://www.espn.com/blog/boston/high-school/post/_/id/30107/texans-williams-gets-number-retired-at-cm |title=Texans' Williams gets number retired at CM |last=Hall |first=Brendan C. |website=ESPN.com |date=February 15, 2014 |access-date=July 25, 2016}} ==Football career== [[File:Brennan Williams (8179300017) (cropped).jpg|thumb|170px|Williams with [[North Carolina Tar Heels football|North Carolina]] in 2012.|left]] ===College=== Williams received an athletic scholarship to attend the [[University of North Carolina at Chapel Hill]], where he played for the [[North Carolina Tar Heels football]] team from 2009 to 2012. As a senior in 2012, he received honorable mention [[List of All-Atlantic Coast Conference football teams|All-Atlantic Coast Conference]] (ACC) honors. Williams tore his labrum his senior year of college.{{cite web|title=Brennan Williams, OT|url=http://www.cbssports.com/nfl/draft/players/1664351/brennan-williams|work=[[CBS Sports]]|access-date=April 28, 2013}} Williams majored in communications while attending North Carolina.{{cite web|title=Brennan Williams|url=http://www.goheels.com/fls/3350/Football/Williams,B_Bio.pdf?SPID=12962&DB_OEM_ID=3350|publisher=UNC|access-date=April 28, 2013|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160303232012/http://www.goheels.com/fls/3350/Football/Williams,B_Bio.pdf?SPID=12962&DB_OEM_ID=3350|archive-date=March 3, 2016|url-status=dead}} ===Professional=== ====Houston Texans==== The [[Houston Texans]] selected Williams in the third round with the 89th overall pick of the [[2013 NFL draft]].{{Cite web |title=2013 NFL Draft Listing |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/years/2013/draft.htm |access-date=May 14, 2023 |website=Pro-Football-Reference.com |language=en}} He would go on to miss his [[rookie]] season with a [[Bone fracture|microfracture]] in his knee. On July 21, 2014, he was released.{{cite news |last=Hanzus |first=Dan |title=Brennan Williams released by Houston Texans |url=https://www.nfl.com/news/brennan-williams-released-by-houston-texans-0ap2000000367044 |access-date=July 24, 2014 |newspaper=National Football League |date=July 21, 2014}} ====Jacksonville Jaguars==== On February 20, 2015, Williams was signed by the [[Jacksonville Jaguars]], to a two-year contract, with the intention of being a backup to starter [[Jermey Parnell]].{{cite web |url=http://www.foxsports.com/nfl/story/jaguars-brennan-williams-finally-close-to-fully-healthy-060915 |title=Jaguars' Brennan Williams finally close to fully healthy |website=FoxSports.com |date=June 9, 2015 |access-date=July 25, 2016}} On August 29, 2015, Williams was released by Jacksonville.{{cite web |title=Jaguars Make Roster Move |url=http://www.jaguars.com/news/article-JaguarsNews/Jaguars-Make-Roster-Move/abe13f2d-4b70-4016-8664-8701aea19622 |website=Jaguars.com |access-date=February 26, 2015 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150223011527/http://www.jaguars.com/news/article-JaguarsNews/Jaguars-Make-Roster-Move/abe13f2d-4b70-4016-8664-8701aea19622 |archive-date=February 23, 2015 |url-status=dead }} ====New England Patriots==== On October 20, 2015, the [[New England Patriots]] signed Williams to their [[practice squad]]. They [[Waivers (American football)|waived]] him two days later.{{cite web |url=http://www.nesn.com/2015/10/brennan-williams-released-by-patriots-will-pursue-dream-of-joining-wwe/ |title=Brennan Williams Released By Patriots, Will Pursue Dream Of Joining WWE |website=NESN.com |last=Kyed |first=Doug |date=October 22, 2015 |access-date=July 25, 2016}} ==Professional wrestling career== ===Reality of Wrestling (2016)=== After being released by the Patriots, Williams returned to [[Houston]] to train to become a professional wrestler under the tutelage of [[WWE]] star [[Booker T (wrestler)|Booker T]].{{cite news|title=WWE Legend Booker T Training Ex-NFLer for Wrestling Stardom|url=http://www.tmz.com/2015/10/25/wwe-booker-t-brennan-williams-wrestling-training/|newspaper=TMZ|access-date=December 15, 2015|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160211171933/http://www.tmz.com/2015/10/25/wwe-booker-t-brennan-williams-wrestling-training|archive-date=February 11, 2016|url-status=live}} He made his debut with Booker's [[Reality of Wrestling]] promotion on February 1, 2016, under the ring name of '''Marcellus Black'''. === WWE (2016–2023) === ==== Early appearances (2016–2020) ==== On February 11, 2016, Williams participated in a WWE try-out at the [[WWE Performance Center]] in [[Orlando, Florida]].{{cite web|url=http://www.houstonpress.com/news/former-houston-texan-brennan-williams-makes-his-pro-wrestling-debut-8150960|title=Former Houston Texan Brenna Williams Makes His Pro Wrestling Debut|website=HoustonPress.com|last=Pendergast|first=Sean|date=February 12, 2016|access-date=July 25, 2016}} On August 1, 2016, WWE officially announced the signing of Williams, who started training at the Performance Center the same day.{{cite web|title=WWE signs former NFL lineman Brennan Williams|url=http://www.f4wonline.com/wwe-news/wwe-signs-former-nfl-lineman-brennan-williams-217731|last=Meltzer|first=Dave|author-link=Dave Meltzer|date=August 1, 2016|access-date=August 1, 2016|work=[[Wrestling Observer Newsletter]]}}{{cite web|last1=Clapp|first1=John|title=WWE signs former NFL player Brennan Williams|url=http://www.wwe.com/shows/wwenxt/article/wwe-signs-brennan-williams|work=WWE|date=August 1, 2016|access-date=August 2, 2016}} He made his in-ring debut for the company at a [[NXT (WWE brand)|NXT]] [[house show|live event]] in Orlando, Florida, on September 30, 2016, competing in a battle royal.{{cite web|url=http://www.pwtorch.com/site/2016/09/30/930-wwe-nxt-results-orlando-team-nakamura-main-event-asuka-itami-15-man-battle-royal-william-regal-appears/|title=9/30 WWE NXT Results in Orlando – Team Nakamura main event, Asuka, Itami, 15-man battle royal, William Regal appears|work=PWTorch|date=October 2016|access-date=October 6, 2016}} In June 2019, Brennan was given the new ring name, '''Dio Maddin'''. On September 10, Maddin joined the commentary team for ''[[WWE 205 Live|205 Live]]'', replacing [[Nigel McGuinness]].{{cite web|url=https://www.prowrestlingsheet.com/dio-maddin-205-live-commentary/#.XXj4N1PTWdM|title=Dio Maddin Joins 205 Live Commentary Team|work=Pro Wrestling Sheet|date=September 11, 2019|access-date=September 11, 2019}} Later that same month, WWE announced as part of their "Premiere Week" that the commentary teams would be changed, with Maddin becoming an analyst for the ''[[WWE Raw|Raw]]'' commentary team with [[Vic Joseph]] and [[Jerry Lawler]]. His work as commentator ended in November 2019, when he was sent back to NXT to train as a wrestler. His absence was explained when, on the November 4, 2019, edition of ''Raw'', Maddin was attacked by [[Brock Lesnar]] who performed an [[Facebuster#Fireman's carry facebuster|F-5]] on Maddin through the announcer's table.{{Cite web|url=https://www.wwe.com/videos/brock-lesnar-mauls-dio-maddin-raw-nov-4-2019|title=Brock Lesnar attacks Raw announcer Dio Maddin }} ==== Retribution (2020–2022) ==== {{main|Retribution (professional wrestling)|l1=Retribution}} On the September 21, 2020, episode of ''Raw'', he made his main roster debut. Now as a wrestler, he was revealed as a member of the [[Heel (professional wrestling)|villainous]] stable [[Retribution (professional wrestling)|Retribution]], under the [[ring name]] '''Mace''', with a mask, new outfit, and sporting a noticeably lighter and more defined physique.{{cite news |title=WWE RAW: Mia Yim, Dio Maddin, Mercedes Martinez, Dominik Dijakovic, y Shane Thorne debutan en la empresa como RETRIBUTION |url=https://solowrestling.mundodeportivo.com/new/92543-wwe-revela-integrantes-retribution-wwe-raw |access-date=January 23, 2021 |work=Solowrestling |date=September 22, 2020 |language=es |archive-date=October 6, 2020 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20201006021512/https://solowrestling.mundodeportivo.com/new/92543-wwe-revela-integrantes-retribution-wwe-raw |url-status=dead }} On the October 5 episode of ''Raw'', [[Mustafa Ali]] revealed as the stable's leader. At [[Fastlane (2021)|Fastlane]] on March 21, 2021, Mace and [[Dijak|T-Bar]] attacked Ali, disbanding the stable. On the April 12 episode of ''Raw'', Mace and T-Bar attacked [[Drew McIntyre]]. The following week on ''Raw'', Mace was finally unmasked along with T-Bar in a tag team match against McIntyre and [[Braun Strowman]], in which Mace and T-Bar won by disqualification. Later in an interview, they confirmed the start of their tag team run. As part of the [[2021 WWE Draft|2021 Draft]], Mace was selected to the [[SmackDown (WWE brand)|SmackDown]] [[WWE brand extension|brand]] while T-Bar remained on the [[Raw (WWE brand)|Raw]] brand, thus disbanding the team.{{Cite web|url=https://www.wwe.com/shows/smackdown/article/latest-wwe-draft-results-2021|title = See all the results from the 2021 Draft}} ==== Maximum Male Models (2022–2023) ==== {{Main|Maximum Male Models}} On the April 15, 2022, episode of ''SmackDown'', Mace returned in a dark segment as [[LA Knight]]'s first acquisition under [[MxM (professional wrestling)|Knight Model Management]]. Following the announcement, Mace defeated [[Erik (wrestler)|Erik]] of [[The Viking Raiders]] in a dark match.{{cite news |last=Rose |first=Bryan |date=April 19, 2022 |title=LA Knight manages Mace in WWE SmackDown dark match |url=https://www.f4wonline.com/.amp/news/wwe/la-knight-appears-in-dark-match-as-manager-prior-to-wwe-smackdown |website=[[Wrestling Observer Newsletter]] |access-date=April 19, 2022}} On the July 1 episode of ''SmackDown'', Knight, now known as Max Dupri, announced Mace and [[Mansoor (wrestler)|Mansoor]], under the tweaked names '''ma.çé''' and mån.sôör, as his new tag team, Maximum Male Models.{{cite news |last=Rose |first=Bryan |date=July 1, 2022 |title=Max Dupri reveals Maximum Male Models on WWE SmackDown |url=https://www.f4wonline.com/.amp/news/wwe/max-dupri-reveals-maximum-male-models-on-wwe-smackdown |website=[[Wrestling Observer Newsletter]] |access-date=July 1, 2022}} Maximum Male Models later welcomed [[Maxxine Dupri]], Max's (kayfabe) sister, to manage the team. Maximum Male Models joined the Raw brand on February 6, 2023, and remained on Raw following the [[2023 WWE Draft]].{{Citation |title=Chelsea Green is unsatisfied with how she has been treated: Raw, Feb. 6, 2023 | date=February 6, 2023 |url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=kBvHEQyT4eQ |language=en |access-date=}}{{cite web |last=Aguilar |first=Matthew |date=May 2, 2023 |title=Every Pick of the 2023 WWE Draft |url=https://comicbook.com/wwe/news/wwe-draft-every-superstar-drafted-night-1-and-2-smackdown-raw/ |access-date=May 2, 2023 |work=[[ComicBook.com]]}} After weeks of spending time with [[Otis (wrestler)|Otis]] of the [[Alpha Academy]], Maxxine left Maximum Male Models to join Alpha Academy on the May 15 episode of ''Raw'' when she cheered on Otis and [[Chad Gable]] eliminating ma.çé and mån.sôör in the [[WWE Intercontinental Championship|Intercontinental Championship]] number one contenders' [[Battle royal (professional wrestling)|battle royal match]].{{Cite web |last=Quinlan |first=Olivia |date=May 15, 2023 |title=WWE Raw Results (05/15) - Cody Rhodes Answers Brock Lesnar's Challenge, We Hear From Becky Lynch And More |url=https://www.wrestlinginc.com/1286771/wwe-raw-live-coverage-0512-cody-rhodes-answers-brock-lesnars-challenge-we-hear-from-becky-lynch-and-more/ |access-date=June 20, 2023 |website=Wrestling Inc. |language=en-US}}{{Citation |title=Alpha Academy eliminate the Maximum Male Models | date=May 18, 2023 |url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=UjWaIIAnfmI |access-date=June 20, 2023 |language=en}} After months of inactivity, ma.çé and mån.sôör both announced on [[Twitter|X]] that they were no longer with WWE on September 21.{{Cite web |last=Yanofsky |first=Daniel |date=September 21, 2023 |title=WWE releases and roster cuts 2023: Dolph Ziggler, Mustafa Ali, Elias headline full list after TKO Group takeover |url=https://www.sportingnews.com/us/wwe/news/wwe-nxt-releases-2023-full-list-cuts-roster/a4d0b8232c1899aa3bfc7468 |access-date=September 21, 2023 |website=www.sportingnews.com |language=en-us}} === Independent circuit (2023–present) === Madden made a surprise appearance at [[Deadlock Pro-Wrestling]] (DPW) [[List of Deadlock Pro-Wrestling events#2nd Anniversary|2nd Anniversary]] taping on December 10, 2023, alongside Mansoor as part of the tag team MxM.{{Cite news |last=Tessier |first=Colin |date=December 10, 2023 |title=Mace And Mansoor Make Surprise Appearance At DPW 2nd Anniversary |url=https://www.fightful.com/wrestling/mace-and-mansoor-make-surprise-appearance-dpw-2nd-anniversary |work=Fightful |access-date=December 11, 2023}}{{Cite news |last=Tessier |first=Colin |date=December 11, 2023 |title=Mace And Mansoor Make First Post-WWE Appearance At DPW 2nd Anniversary |url=https://www.wrestlezone.com/news/1428265-mace-and-mansoor-make-first-post-wwe-appearance-at-dpw-2nd-anniversary |work=Wrestlezone |access-date=December 11, 2023}} MxM made their in ring debut for DPW at ''DPW Live 4'' on January 20, 2024.{{Cite tweet |number=1736473740584665525 |user=deadlockpro |title=🚨 DPW L4 UPDATE 🚨 MXM make their in-ring DPW debut against WEST COAST WRECKING CREW in a tag team grudge bout on January 20th in Raleigh! DPW LIVE 4 🗓️ 01/20 {{!}} Raleigh, NC 🎟 http://dpwtix.com |date=December 18, 2023 |access-date=December 20, 2023}} On April 13, MxM appeared for the [[Uganda]]n-based [[Soft Ground Wrestling]] (SGW) promotion, with their appearance helping give the rising promotion further notoriety, with many other wrestlers from promotions such as [[All Elite Wrestling|AEW]] and [[Total Nonstop Action Wrestling|TNA]] showing their support for both the team and the promotion itself.{{Cite news |last=Lambert |first=Jeremy |date=April 18, 2024 |title=Maximum Male Models Make SGW Debut, Confront Lord White |url=https://www.fightful.com/wrestling/mxm-make-sgw-debut-confront-lord-white?utm_source=TW-Fightful&utm_medium=Fightful%20Wrestling%20News&utm_campaign=dlvr.it |access-date=April 28, 2024 |work=Fightful}} === All Elite Wrestling / Ring of Honor (2024–present) === {{Main|MxM Collection|l1 = MxM TV}} Madden and Mansoor, as MxM Collection, made their [[Ring of Honor]] (ROH) debut on the July 4, 2024 episode of ''[[Ring of Honor Wrestling]]'' in a pre-taped vignette.{{Cite news |last=Defelice |first=Robert |date=July 4, 2024 |title=MxM Collection (Mason Madden And Mansoor) Arrive In Ring Of Honor With Vignette On 7/4/24 ROH |url=https://www.fightful.com/wrestling/mxm-collection-mason-madden-and-mansoor-arrive-ring-honor-vignette-7424-roh |work=Fightful |access-date=July 11, 2024}} On July 10, it was reported that MxM Collection had signed a deal with ROH and its sister promotion [[All Elite Wrestling]] (AEW).{{Cite web |last=Thomas |first=Jeremy |date=July 10, 2024 |title=MxM Reportedly Signed With AEW & ROH |url=https://411mania.com/wrestling/mxm-reportedly-signed-aew-roh/ |website=411 Mania |access-date=July 11, 2024}} MxM Collection made their ROH in-ring debut at [[Death Before Dishonor (2024)|Death Before Dishonor]]: ''Zero Hour'' on July 26 defeating Spanish Announce Project ([[Angélico]] and [[Serpentico]]).{{Cite web |last=Powell |first=Jason |date=July 26, 2024 |title=ROH Death Before Dishonor results: Vetter's review of Mark Briscoe vs. Roderick Strong for the ROH Championship, Athena vs. Queen Aminata for the ROH Women's Championship |url=https://prowrestling.net/site/2024/07/26/roh-death-before-dishonor-results-vetters-review-of-mark-briscoe-vs-roderick-strong-for-the-roh-championship-athena-vs-queen-aminata-for-the-roh-womens-championship/ |access-date=July 27, 2024 |website=Pro Wrestling Dot Net |language=}} MxM Collection made their AEW debut on the July 27 episode of ''[[AEW Collision]]'', in a losing effort against [[FTR (professional wrestling)|FTR]] ([[Cash Wheeler]] and [[Dax Harwood]]).{{Cite news |last=Mrosko |first=Geno |date=July 27, 2024 |title=AEW Collision & Battle of the Belts 11 results, live blog |url=https://www.cagesideseats.com/aew/2024/7/27/24207720/aew-collision-battle-of-the-belts-11-results-live-blog |website=Cageside Seats |access-date=July 28, 2024 |archive-date=July 27, 2024 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240727233735/https://www.cagesideseats.com/aew/2024/7/27/24207720/aew-collision-battle-of-the-belts-11-results-live-blog |url-status=dead }} On the November 6, episode of ''Collision'', MxM Collection formed an alliance with [[Johnny TV]].{{Cite news |last=Lambert |first=Jeremy |date=November 2, 2024 |title=MxM Collection Are The Gift That Gives And Receives, Johnny TV Tells Them To Slide Into His DMs |url=https://www.fightful.com/wrestling/mxm-collection-are-gift-gives-and-receives-johnny-tv-tells-them-slide-his-dms |work=Fightful News |access-date=December 2, 2024}} At the [[AEW Revolution (2025)|Revolution]] pre-show on March 9, 2025, TV and MxM Collection lost to [[A.J. & Big Justice|"Big Boom!" A.J.]], [[Orange Cassidy]] and [[Mark Briscoe]] in a trios match.{{cite web |last=Powell |first=Jason |date=March 9, 2025 |title=AEW Revolution pre-show results: Big Boom AJ, Orange Cassidy, and Mark Briscoe vs. Johnny TV, Mason Madden, and Mansoor, Chris Jericho vs. Gravity for the ROH Championship |url=https://prowrestling.net/site/2025/03/09/aew-revolution-pre-show-results-big-boom-aj-orange-cassidy-and-mark-briscoe-vs-johnny-tv-mason-madden-and-mansoor-chris-jericho-vs-gravity-for-the-roh-championship/ |access-date=March 9, 2025 |work=Pro Wrestling Dot Net}} TV and MxM Collection were later joined by TV's real-life wife [[Taya Valkyrie]], renaming MxM Collection to MxM TV.{{Cite web |title=ROH on HonorClub #131 « Events Database « CAGEMATCH - The Internet Wrestling Database |url=https://www.cagematch.net/?id=1&nr=431683 |access-date=October 25, 2025 |website=www.cagematch.net}}{{Cite web |title=MxM TV « Stables Database « CAGEMATCH - The Internet Wrestling Database |url=https://www.cagematch.net/?id=29&nr=4481&name=MxM+TV |access-date=October 25, 2025 |website=www.cagematch.net}} === DDT Pro-Wrestling (2025–present) === On June 29, 2025, at [[DDT King of Kings|King of Kings]], MxM Collection made their [[DDT Pro-Wrestling]] debut, defeating [[Danshoku Dino]] and [[Kazuki Hirata]].{{Cite web |title=MxM Collection Making DDT Pro-Wrestling Debut At June 29th Korakuen Hall Show {{!}} Fightful News |url=https://www.fightful.com/wrestling/mxm-collection-making-ddt-pro-wrestling-debut-june-29th-korakuen-hall-show |access-date=June 30, 2025 |website=www.fightful.com |date=May 29, 2025 |language=en}}{{Cite web |title=DDT King Of Kings 2025 ~ Arashi's June Showdown ~ « Events Database « CAGEMATCH - The Internet Wrestling Database |url=https://www.cagematch.net/?id=1&nr=429057 |access-date=June 30, 2025 |website=www.cagematch.net}} ==Personal life== Williams is the son of Jacquelyn and former NFL defensive end [[Brent Williams (American football)|Brent Williams]]. He has three children with his wife Ciarra.{{cite web|url=https://www.houstonpress.com/news/plan-b-brennan-williams-hopes-to-turn-his-nfl-disappointment-into-a-wrestling-career-7932302|title=Plan B: Brennan Williams Hopes to Turn His NFL Disappointment Into a Wrestling Career|first=Sean|last=Pendergast|publisher=HoustonPRess|date=November 17, 2015|access-date=April 16, 2019}} His brother Cam played as a linebacker for [[Ohio State Buckeyes football|Ohio State]] and became a scout for the [[New England Patriots]].{{cite web|url=https://www.cleveland.com/osu/2016/02/cam_williams_former_ohio_state.html|title=Cam Williams, former Ohio State linebacker, accepts scout job with New England Patriots |work=cleveland.com|first=Bill|last=Landis|date=February 3, 2016}} His younger sister Jaylen, a former basketball player at Penn State,{{Cite web|url=https://gopsusports.com/sports/womens-basketball/roster/jaylen-williams/5291|title = Jaylen Williams - Women's Basketball}} signed with the WWE from August 19, 2021, until April 29, 2022.{{cite web | last=Winnard | first=Liam | title=Here's Who WWE Hired At Latest Tryouts | website=WrestleTalk | date=August 20, 2021 | url=https://wrestletalk.com/news/who-wwe-hired-latest-tryouts/ | access-date=November 11, 2024}}{{Cite news |last1=Lambert |first1=Jeremy |last2=Guzzo |first2=Gisberto |date=April 30, 2022 |title=Raelyn Divine Released By WWE, Posts Comment Saying She's Still In Love With Wrestling |url=https://www.fightful.com/wrestling/raelyn-divine-released-wwe |work=Fightful |access-date=December 11, 2023}} Williams has been a fan of professional wrestling growing up, citing [[Eddie Guerrero]] and [[Keiji Muto|The Great Muta]] as some of his favorite wrestlers. He is also a fan of [[video games]], [[anime]] and [[manga]].{{cite news|url=https://www.si.com/extra-mustard/2015/07/17/jaguars-brennan-williams-anime-wwe-marvel-comics|title=Catching up with Jaguars OL Brennan Williams: The NFL's biggest nerd|first=Luke|last=Winkie|newspaper=Sports Illustrated |date=July 17, 2015 }} His love for anime is part of his wrestling gimmick, with his running knee attack named "Nico Nico Knee", a play on the catchphrase "Nico Nico Nii" which belongs to the character Nico Yazawa from the anime ''[[Love Live!]]''.[https://www.animenewsnetwork.com/interest/2022-03-10/love-live-reference-makes-it-into-wwe-2k22-game/.183412 Anime News Network: "Love Live! Reference Makes It Into WWE 2K22 Game"] ==Other media== {{Infobox social media personality | name = JiBo VT | youtube_id = UCASTxVYeQ3uvT8qdIlHx-oA | youtube_display_name = JiBoVT | youtube_years_active = 2021–present | youtube_genre = [[VTuber]] | youtube_subscribers = 12.2 thousand | youtube_views = 872.4 thousand | stats_update = March 30, 2025 }} Williams has appeared in various streams on the tabletop role-playing YouTube channel The Third Wheel, most notably in the role of The Batsu Sama, the scariest person in the world.{{cite web |url=https://www.youtube.com/channel/UCd83kSpJ-jJGCE_L8Yaoakg |title=The Third Wheel|via=[[YouTube]]}}{{cite web |url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=UD6Vjr5KLqQ |title=TENRA BANSHO ZERO - The Book of a Thousand Destinies|via=[[YouTube]]|date=June 5, 2016 }} He joined the main series of the channel "Thrilling Intent", as a steely alchemist named Harlock, with a bionic arm and a love for traps, as well as another series on the channel, No Smarts But Hearts, where he plays the prestigious Clover Von Krone, a warm-natured, but incredibly strong member with the elite Adventurer Knights.{{cite web |url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=qA_FeiuM10k&t=24s |title=Thrilling Intent|via=[[YouTube]]|date=December 27, 2016 }} He also appears on several series on the tabletop role-playing channel Stabbyness, in "Forgotten Indigo", "Carbon Interface", and "Reflection".{{cite web |title=The Crew |url=https://stabbyness.com/the-crew |website=Stabbyness |date=June 6, 2023 }}{{cite web |title=Forgotten Indigo: Third Impact |url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=v5_bAsBDryQ&list=PLIO5L7W1uDs1h73gbehmg0gpOv_6b1erV&index=4 |via=YouTube | date=October 23, 2021 }} Williams took part in multiple collaborations with the YouTube channel Super Best Friends Play, where he earned the nickname "Better Woolie" for his resemblance to group member Woolie Madden, from which his name change to Dio Maddin is partly derived. He also appeared in a Minecraft Wrestling Show called "Minecraft Wrestling Alliance". He has also done voice-over/narration for various videos, such as "Jojo's Bizarre Adventure Part 2" by Did You Know Anime,{{cite web |url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=n8j8ItOJpPA |title=Jojo's Bizarre Adventure Part 2 - Did You Know Anime?|via=[[YouTube]]|date=May 29, 2016 }} and "Welcome to YouTube Comments (2016) - Part 1" by JelloApocalypse.{{cite web |url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=X3pKemjHsuk |title=Welcome to YouTube Comments (2016) - Part 1|via=[[YouTube]]|date=February 10, 2017 }} On February 3, 2021, Williams re-launched his YouTube channel as a [[VTuber]] under the name '''JiBo'''.{{cite magazine|last=D'Anastasio|first=Cecilia|title=He's a WWE Star and a Vtuber. Those Worlds Aren't So Different|url=https://www.wired.com/story/brennan-williams-mace-jibo-wwe-vtubing/|magazine=Wired|date=April 28, 2021|access-date=May 28, 2021}} == Championships and accomplishments == * '''Australian Championship Wrestling''' ** ACW World Tag Team Championship (1 time, current) – with [[Mansoor (wrestler)|Mansoor]]{{cite web |title=ACW World Tag Team Championship |url=https://www.cagematch.net/?id=5&nr=8199 |website=Cagematch |access-date=6 September 2026}} * '''[[Hoodslam]]''' ** Intergalactic Tag Team Championship (1 time) – with Mansoor * '''''[[Pro Wrestling Illustrated]]''''' **Ranked No. 211 of the top 500 singles wrestlers in the ''[[Pro Wrestling Illustrated#PWI 500|PWI 500]]'' in 2021{{cite web|url=http://www.profightdb.com/pwi-500/2021.html|title=Pro Wrestling Illustrated (PWI) 500 for 2021|work=The Internet Wrestling Database|access-date=October 8, 2021}} * '''''[[WrestleCrap]]''''' ** [[WrestleCrap#Gooker Award|Gooker Award]] (2020) – {{small|as part of [[Retribution (professional wrestling)|Retribution]]}}{{cite web|url=https://www.wrestlecrap.com/inductions/retribution/ |url-status=live |archive-url=https://archive.today/20230304113736/https://www.wrestlecrap.com/inductions/retribution/ |archive-date=March 4, 2023 |title=RETRIBUTION The 2020 Gooker Award winner |work=WrestleCrap |last=O'Donnell |first=Art |access-date=March 4, 2023}} * '''''[[Wrestling Observer Newsletter]]''''' ** [[List of Wrestling Observer Newsletter awards#Worst Gimmick|Worst Gimmick]] '''Michael Eric Reid''' (born December 30, 1992) is an American actor and comedian. He is best known for his role as Sinjin Van Cleef in ''[[Victorious]]''.

== Career ==
He has appeared on ''[[Saturday Night Live]]'', ''[[Last Call with Carson Daly]]'', ''[[Late Show with David Letterman]]'' and other television shows. From 2010 to 2013, he played Sinjin Van Cleef on ''[[Victorious (TV series)|Victorious]]'', a role he has been best remembered for.<ref>{{cite web|last=Prommer|first=Stephanie|title=Interview with Actor Mikey Reid|url=http://teenfashion.about.com/od/celebritystyle/tp/MikeyReidInterview.htm|publisher=About.com Teen Fashion|accessdate=10 September 2013|archive-date=4 December 2013|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20131204121252/http://teenfashion.about.com/od/celebritystyle/tp/MikeyReidInterview.htm|url-status=dead}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|title=Mikey Reid From Victorious Hits the Orange Carpet|url=http://www.nick.com/news/kca-2011-mikey-reid-interview.html|publisher=Nickelodeon|accessdate=10 September 2013}}</ref> Reid appeared in ''[[Mamaboy]]'' as Ditto, the best friend of the lead character Kelly Hankins, a high school student who must hide the fact that he has become pregnant.<ref>http://www.mamaboythemovie.com {{webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20151222103932/http://www.mamaboythemovie.com/ | date=2015-12-22}}</ref>

==Personal life==

'''Nicole Muñoz''' (born June 24, 1994<ref name="Hollywood.com">{{cite web |url=http://www.hollywood.com/celebrities/nicole-munoz-58518262/ |title=Nicole Munoz |website=Hollywood.com |accessdate=June 25, 2016}}</ref>) is a Canadian film and television actress. She is known for her roles as Pamela (Pammy) Wagner in the film ''[[The Tooth Fairy (film)|The Tooth Fairy]]'', as Young Cody in the film ''[[Fetching Cody]]'', and for her role as Christie Tarr (née McCawley) in the [[Syfy]] television series ''[[Defiance (TV series)|Defiance]]''. In 2019, Muñoz began starring as Jack in season 4 of Syfy series ''[[Van Helsing (TV series)|Van Helsing]]''.<ref name=":0" />

==Early and personal life==
Muñoz was born in [[Vancouver]], [[British Columbia]] to a Spanish father and a Québécois mother.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://twitter.com/NicoleMunoz94/status/609449464038711297|title=My dad is from Spain and my mom was born in Quebec.|publisher=Nicole Muñoz|via=Twitter|date=12 June 2015|access-date=15 November 2019}}</ref> She has two sisters, Britta and Sophia.<ref name="Hollywood.com" /> She moved to [[Toronto]] when she was cast in ''[[Defiance (TV series)|Defiance]]'' at age 18.<ref>{{cite journal|url=https://hiplatina.com/listen-in-to-our-conversation-with-actress-nicole-munoz-from-defiance/|title=Listen In To Our Conversation With Actress Nicole Muñoz from "Defiance"|journal=Hip Latina|date=July 20, 2015|accessdate=November 15, 2019}}</ref>

==Career==
Muñoz has over 60 commercial spots and 40 film and TV credits to her name.<ref>[http://www.tvsa.co.za/actorprofile.asp?actorID=15778 Nicole Muñoz]</ref> She made her television debut in an episode of ''[[Jeremiah (TV series)|Jeremiah]]''. She also made guest appearances on many TV shows including, ''[[Da Vinci's Inquest]]'', ''[[Tru Calling]]'', ''[[The Dead Zone (TV series)|Stephen King's Dead Zone]]'', ''[[Stargate: Atlantis]]'' and ''[[Supernatural (American TV series)|Supernatural]]''. She got her first recurring role in  2009 in the space travel, television science fiction drama series, ''[[Defying Gravity (TV series)|Defying Gravity]]'' playing a Palestinian girl. In 2006 and 2007, she appeared in 4 [[made-for-television]] movies as well. In 2009, she made a guest appearance on [[Syfy]] series, ''[[Sanctuary (Canadian TV series)|Sanctuary]]'' episode, [[Pavor Nocturnus (Sanctuary)|Pavor Nocturnus]] playing Jessica Mitchell, a young girl lost in a post-apocalyptic world.

Muñoz has also played small roles in big-budget movies shot in Canada including ''[[Fantastic Four (2005 film)|Fantastic Four]]'', ''[[Pathfinder (2007 film)|Pathfinder]]'', ''[[Another Cinderella Story]]'', ''[[Center Stage: Turn It Up]]'' and the [[Dwayne Johnson]] starrer, ''[[Tooth Fairy (2010 film)|Tooth Fairy]]''. Her other films include [[HBO]] thriller ''[[Imaginary Playmate]]'', and ''[[The Last Mimzy]]'', for which she was one of the nominees for the [[29th Young Artist Awards]] category, ''Best Performance by a Young Ensemble Cast''. In mid-2012, she was cast in ''[[Defiance (TV series)|Defiance]]'' in a recurring role.<ref>{{cite news|last=Willard|first=Erin|title=Syfy's Defiance Begins Production in Toronto; Bear McCreary to Score|url=http://scifimafia.com/2012/04/syfys-defiance-begins-production-in-toronto-bear-mccreary-to-score/|accessdate=September 13, 2013|newspaper=ScifiMafia|date=April 26, 2012|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20130515065311/http://scifimafia.com/2012/04/syfys-defiance-begins-production-in-toronto-bear-mccreary-to-score/|archive-date=May 15, 2013|url-status=dead}}</ref> In 2016 Muñoz was cast opposite [[Laurie Holden]] in ''[[Pyewacket (film)|Pywacket]]'', an occult movie directed by  [[Adam MacDonald]].<ref name="Pyewacket">{{cite web |author=Etan Vlessing |url=http://www.hollywoodreporter.com/news/walking-dead-alum-laurie-holden-star-indie-thriller-pyewacket-941118 |title='Walking Dead' Alum Laurie Holden to Star in Indie Thriller 'Pyewacket' |work=[[The Hollywood Reporter]] |date=October 25, 2016 |access-date=January 10, 2017}}</ref>

In 2019, Muñoz began starring as Jack in season 4 of [[Syfy]] series ''[[Van Helsing (TV series)|Van Helsing]]''.<ref name=":0">{{cite web|url=https://deadline.com/2019/05/van-helsing-tricia-helfer-stakes-claim-to-dracula-role-wwe-wrestling-star-also-added-to-cast-1202614231/|title='Van Helsing': Tricia Helfer Stakes Claim To Dracula Role & WWE Wrestling Star Also Added To Cast|last=Boucher|first=Geoff|website=Deadline Hollywood|date=May 14, 2019|accessdate=May 14, 2019}}</ref>

{{Short description|American television personality (born 1997)}} {{distinguish|Sade Robinson}} {{BLP sources|date=April 2022}} {{Use mdy dates|date=October 2020}} {{Infobox person | name = Sadie Robertson Huff | image = Sadie Robertson (cropped).jpg | caption = Robertson in February 2015 | birth_date = {{birth date and age|1997|06|11|mf=yes}} | birth_name = Sadie Carroway Robertson | birth_place = [[Monroe, Louisiana]], U.S. | television = {{ubl | ''[[Duck Dynasty]]'' | ''[[Dancing with the Stars (U.S. TV series)|Dancing with the Stars]]'' | ''[[Hallmark Channel]]'' }} | education = [[Ouachita Christian High School]] | occupation = Television personality, author, actress | father = [[Willie Robertson]] | children = 3 | mother = [[Korie Robertson]] | spouse = {{marriage|Christian Huff|2019}} | relatives = {{ubl | [[Phil Robertson]] (grandfather) | [[Kay Robertson]] (grandmother) | [[Jase Robertson]] (uncle) | [[Si Robertson]] (great uncle) }} | years_active = 2012–present }} '''Sadie Carroway Robertson Huff''' ({{nee|''Robertson''}}; born June 11, 1997) is an American Christian speaker, actress, businesswoman, podcaster, and author. She rose to fame on the [[A&E (TV network)|A&E]] reality television show ''[[Duck Dynasty]]''. She is a prominent Christian social media personality, host of ''WHOA, That's Good'' podcast, and founder of the ministry ''Live Original''.{{Cite web |date=2018-08-03 |title=About - Live Original |url=https://liveoriginal.com/about/ |access-date=2025-04-22 |language=en-US}} ==Early life== Robertson Huff is a granddaughter of [[Phil Robertson]], founder of [[Duck Commander]]. Her parents are [[Korie Robertson]] (née Howard) and [[Willie Robertson]], the company's current CEO. She has five siblings: John Luke Robertson, Rebecca Loflin, Willie Robertson Jr., Bella Robertson-Mayo, and Rowdy Robertson.{{citation needed|date= July 2023}} ==Career== [[File:Sadie Robertson 2014.jpg|thumb|left|upright|Robertson in 2014]] She sang ''[[Away in a Manger]]'' with [[Alison Krauss]] for her family's bestselling album, ''[[Duck the Halls: A Robertson Family Christmas]]''.{{cite web|url=http://www.noladefender.com/content/duck-dynasty-christmas-album-tops-charts |title=Duck Dynasty Christmas Album Tops the Charts |publisher=Nola Defender |date=2013-11-24 |access-date=2013-12-21}}{{cite web|url=http://www.fuse.tv/2013/12/christmas-2013-duck-dynasty-album-interview |title='Duck Dynasty' Stars React to Their Xmas Album Outselling Gaga's 'ARTPOP' - Interview - Fuse |publisher=Fuse.tv |access-date=2013-12-21}} Robertson Huff was the runner-up on Season 19 of ''[[Dancing with the Stars (U.S. TV series)|Dancing with the Stars]].'' Robertson Huff has appeared in two films ''[[God's Not Dead 2]]'' and ''[[I'm Not Ashamed (film)|I'm Not Ashamed]]'', and launched her successful speaking and worship tour, ''Live Original,'' in the fall of 2016.{{Cite journal |last1=Maslanik |first1=Thomas |last2=Tannura |first2=Kate |last3=Mahaffey |first3=Lucas |last4=Loughridge |first4=Alice Brianne |last5=Benninson |first5=Lida |last6=Ursell |first6=Luke |last7=Greenwood |first7=Benjamin N. |last8=Knight |first8=Rob |last9=Fleshner |first9=Monika |date=2012-12-07 |title=Commensal Bacteria and MAMPs Are Necessary for Stress-Induced Increases in IL-1β and IL-18 but Not IL-6, IL-10 or MCP-1 |journal=PLOS ONE |volume=7 |issue=12 |article-number=e50636 |doi=10.1371/journal.pone.0050636 |pmid=23236381 |pmc=3517493 |bibcode=2012PLoSO...750636M |issn=1932-6203 |doi-access=free }} Robertson Huff speaks at Passion Christian Conference every January.{{Cite web |date=2023-02-02 |title=Sadie Robertson Huff - Passion 2023 |url=https://passionconferences.com/message/a-personal-life-with-jesus-sadie-robertson-huff-dallas-ft-worth-tx/ |access-date=2023-08-29 |website=Passion Conferences |language=en-US}}{{Cite web |last1=Alcindor |first1=Nicole |last2=Reporter |first2=C. P. |date=2023-01-09 |title=Sadie Robertson says Christians can't keep personal, spiritual lives separate, calls for repentance |url=https://www.christianpost.com/news/passion-2023-sadie-robertson-leads-prayer-for-repentance.html |access-date=2023-08-29 |website=The Christian Post |language=en-US}} Robertson Huff partnered with Roma Boots and worked alongside them in their mission to "give poverty the boot."{{Cite web |title=Day of Hope: 'giving poverty the boot' |url=https://romaboots.com/pages/day-of-hope |access-date=2023-06-24 |website=Roma Boots}}{{Cite web |date=2016-07-30 |title=Sadie Robertson: Part of the Roma Family |url=https://romaboots.com/blogs/roma-boots-blog/sadie-robertson-part-of-the-roma-family |access-date=2023-06-24 |website=Roma Boots}} In 2014, Robertson Huff wrote a [[The New York Times Best Seller list|''New York Times'' Best Seller]] book about faith and [[Christian values]] called ''Live Original''.{{Cite web|last=Klett|first=Leah Marieann|date=2015-07-29|title='Duck Dynasty' Star Sadie Robertson to Release Line of Christian-Themed Home Decor, Inspirational Jewelry|url=http://www.gospelherald.com/articles/56809/20150729/duck-dynasty-star-sadie-robertson-to-release-line-of-christian-themed-home-decor-inspirational-jewelry.htm|access-date=2022-02-15|website=Breaking Christian News: World, Business, and More {{!}} The Gospel Herald|language=en}} She released a sequel to her first book, ''Live Original'', called ''Live Fearless'', in 2018 and in 2020 released ''Live: Remain Alive, Be Alive at a Specified Time, Have an Exciting or Fulfilling Life''. This book encourages readers to thrive in God-given life, find confidence, deal with haters, live in the moment, discover the power of words, and wholeheartedly embrace God's ways so they can make the best choices.{{Cite web |title=Live by Sadie Robertson Huff |url=https://globalleadership.org/product/live-by-sadie-robertson-huff/ |access-date=2023-08-25 |website=Global Leadership Network |language=en-US}} In 2021, Robertson Huff signed a deal to be part of a TV series titled, ''Life Just Got Real'', with producer [[Brad Krevoy]]. The series idea was adapted from her book, ''Life Just Got Real'', which was published in 2016.{{Cite web |last=Wiseman |first=Andreas |date=2021-05-07 |title='Duck Dynasty' Star Sadie Robertson Huff Returns To Screen With 'Life Just Got Real' Scripted Series; Brad Krevoy Producing |url=https://deadline.com/2021/05/duck-dynasty-sadie-robertson-huff-series-life-just-got-real-1234751844/ |access-date=2024-03-21 |website=Deadline |language=en-US}} Robertson Huff would appear on the show, however, her main role would be that of producer.{{Cite web |title=Duck Dynasty's Sadie Robertson Lands Scripted TV Series for Her Book Life Just Got Real |url=https://people.com/tv/duck-dynasty-sadie-robertson-lands-scripted-tv-series-for-her-book-life-just-got-real/ |access-date=2024-03-21 |website=Peoplemag |language=en}} ''Live on Purpose: 100 Devotionals for Letting Go of Fear and Following God'' was released in September 2021 and in February 2022, she published ''Who Are You Following?: Pursuing Jesus in a Social-Media Obsessed World.''{{Cite web |last=Day |first=Heather Thompson |date=2022-02-11 |title=Sadie Robertson Huff: Who Are You Following? |url=https://www.christianitytoday.com/ct/podcasts/viral-jesus/sadie-robertson-huff-who-are-you-following.html |access-date=2023-08-25 |website=ChristianityToday.com |language=en}} She co wrote a book with her husband entitled ''How to Put Love First: Find Meaningful Connection with God, Your People, and Your Community'' (2023).{{cite web | title=How to Put Love First | website=WorldCat.org | url=https://search.worldcat.org/title/1373607068 | access-date=February 13, 2024}} In February 2024, it was announced that Robertson Huff would be the commencement speaker at the [[University of Mount Olive]] 2024 graduation.{{Cite web |last=staff |first=News Argus |date=2024-02-01 |title=Sadie Robertson-Huff to speak at UMO commencement |url=https://www.newsargus.com/news/local/sadie-robertson-huff-to-speak-at-umo-commencement/article_1da67f3c-cc2c-5f01-9eed-96256ce9b1b5.html |access-date=2024-05-22 |website=Goldsboro News-Argus |language=en}} ==Personal life== In 2018, Robertson Huff dated ''[[Outer Banks (TV series)|Outer Banks]]'' actor [[Austin North]] for four months.{{cite web|title=Who is Austin North dating? |date=16 June 2020 |url=https://www.popsugar.com/Who-Is-Austin-North-Dating-47551959 |publisher=Pop Sugar}} On June 9, 2019, Robertson Huff became engaged to Christian Huff.{{cite magazine|last1=Stone|first1=Natalie|date=June 10, 2019|title=Duck Dynasty's Sadie Robertson Is Engaged to Christian Huff|magazine=[[People (magazine)|People]]|url=https://people.com/tv/sadie-robertson-engaged-christian-huff/}} They married on November 25, 2019.{{Cite magazine|last=Stone|first=Natalie|date=November 25, 2019|title=Sadie Robertson Marries Christian Huff in 'Romantic and Elegant' Louisiana Wedding|url=https://people.com/tv/sadie-robertson-marries-christian-huff/|magazine=[[People (magazine)|People]]|language=EN}} On October 4, 2020, the couple announced that they were expecting their first child, a girl.{{Cite magazine|last=Stone|first=Natalie|date=October 4, 2020|title=Sadie Robertson Expecting First Child with Husband Christian Huff: 'Screaming with Excitement!'|url=https://people.com/parents/sadie-robertson-pregnant-expecting-first-child-with-husband-christian-huff/|magazine=[[People (magazine)|People]]|language=EN}} On May 11, 2021, Robertson Huff gave birth to their daughter.{{cite web |last1=Emmanuele |first1=Julia |title=Sadie Robertson and Christian Huff: A Timeline of Their Relationship |url=https://www.usmagazine.com/celebrity-news/pictures/sadie-robertson-and-christian-huffs-relationship-timeline/may-2021-139/ |website=Us Weekly |access-date=3 November 2022 |date=6 February 2022}}{{Cite web |last=McCarty |first=India |date=2025-04-22 |title=Sadie Robertson Huff Reminds Us of the Power of Words: 'Not a Small Thing' |url=https://www.movieguide.org/news-articles/sadie-robertson-huff-reminds-us-of-the-power-of-words.html |access-date=2025-04-22 |website=Movieguide {{!}} The Family Guide to Movies & Entertainment |language=en-US}} On November 3, 2022, they announced that they were expecting their second child. Their daughter was born on May 22, 2023.{{Cite web |date=2022-11-06 |title=Duck Dynasty's Sadie Robertson Huff Announces 'A Little Miracle Is In Motion' |url=https://www2.cbn.com/news/entertainment/duck-dynastys-sadie-robertson-huff-announces-little-miracle-motion |access-date=2023-09-19 |website=CBN |language=en}}{{cite web | url=https://www.eonline.com/news/1353329/sadie-robertson-is-pregnant-expecting-baby-no-2-with-christian-huff | title=Sadie Robertson is Pregnant, Expecting Baby No. 2 with Christian Huff | date=November 4, 2022 }} On February 14, 2025, they announced that she was expecting their third child.{{Cite web|last=Stivale|first=Shelby|date=February 14, 2025|title=Duck Dynasty's Sadie Robertson Expecting Baby No. 3 With Husband Christian Huff|url=https://www.usmagazine.com/celebrity-moms/news/duck-dynastys-sadie-robertson-christian-huff-expecting-baby-no-3/|publisher=[[Us Weekly]]}} On August 1, 2025, the couple welcomed their third child, a daughter.{{Cite web |title=Sadie Robertson Welcomes Baby No. 3 with Husband Christian Huff |url=https://people.com/sadie-robertson-welcomes-baby-no-3-with-husband-christian-huff-11773819 |access-date=2025-08-04 |website=People.com |language=en}} ==Filmography== {| class="wikitable sortable" |+ Film ! He currently competes in the [[Heavyweight (MMA)|Heavyweight]] division of the [[Ultimate Fighting Championship]] (UFC), where he is the former two-time [[List of UFC champions#Light Heavyweight Championship|UFC Light Heavyweight Champion]] and former [[List of UFC champions#Middleweight Championship|UFC Middleweight Champion]]. In kickboxing, he is a former [[Glory (kickboxing)|Glory]] [[Glory (kickboxing)#Glory Middleweight Championship|middleweight]] and [[Glory (kickboxing)#Glory Light Heavyweight Championship|light heavyweight]] champion, and is the first and only fighter to have held Glory titles in two weight classes simultaneously. In 2009 at 21 years old, he began training [[kickboxing]] in order to get rid of his addiction. After several unsuccessful attempts to control his addiction, he stopped drinking alcohol permanently at the end of 2012.{{cite web|url=https://www.mmafighting.com/2020/11/20/21573867/alex-pereira-born-to-fight-battle-against-alcoholism-lfa-glory|title=Alex Pereira found out he was 'born to fight' during battle against alcoholism|author=Guilherme Cruz|date=November 20, 2020|publisher=mmafighting.com|access-date=24 March 2021|archive-date=20 November 2020|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20201120185744/https://www.mmafighting.com/2020/11/20/21573867/alex-pereira-born-to-fight-battle-against-alcoholism-lfa-glory|url-status=live}} Upon joining Master Belocqua Wera's academy, he discovered his natural talent for martial arts. ==Amateur boxing career== Before becoming a prominent figure in kickboxing and mixed martial arts, Alex Pereira had a notable amateur boxing career in [[Brazil]]. He reportedly competed in 28 amateur boxing matches, achieving a record of 25 wins, all by knockout, with just 3 losses.{{cite web|url=https://talksport.com/boxing/2047565/jake-paul-alex-pereira-amateur-boxing-footage-ufc/|title='He stands no chance' – Jake Paul urged not to fight Alex Pereira after terrifying amateur boxing footage emerges of UFC star flatlining opponents|date= September 12, 2024|magazine=[[Talksport]]|access-date=October 3, 2024}} Pereira’s signature power, particularly his devastating left hook, became evident early in his amateur career, as seen in viral footage showcasing multiple knockouts, including an instance where he knocked an opponent out of the ring.{{cite web|url=https://bloodyelbow.com/2024/09/12/ryan-garcia-says-hed-love-to-train-with-alex-pereira-after-watching-the-ufc-champions-terrifying-amateur-boxing-highlights/|title=Ryan Garcia says he'd 'love to train' with Alex Pereira after watching the UFC champion's terrifying amateur boxing highlights|date= September 12, 2024|magazine=[[Bloody Elbow]]|access-date=October 3, 2024}} ==Kickboxing career== In 2012 Alex won the [[Jungle Fight]] Middleweight Title, the WGP -85 kg/187 lb Championship and challenged for the [[It's Showtime (kickboxing)|''It's Showtime'']] 85MAX Championship vs [[Jason Wilnis]] losing by TKO in the second round. In 2013 he won the [[World Association of Kickboxing Organizations|WAKO]] Pro Panamerican K-1 -85 kg/187 lb Championship. In late 2013 he went back to the amateurs to participate in the W.A.K.O. [[W.A.K.O. World Championships 2013|World Championship]] '13 at -91 kg. He won in the quarter final and the semi final but came up short in the finals vs [[Sergej Maslobojev]] earning him a silver medal. Two months later he participated in the WGP tournament and beat Camilo Ferraz in the semi final and fought [[César Almeida (fighter)|César Almeida]] in the finals having previously defeating him in [[Superkombat Fighting Championship|SUPERKOMBAT New Heroes 2]], in the finals Alex lost by decision making their rivalry 1-1. '''LaKeisha Moore''' (born June 3, 1987) is an American [[Sprint (running)|sprinter]].<ref name="Bio">{{cite web |url=http://www.iaaf.org/athletes/united-states/lakeisha-lawson-242156 |title=LaKeisha Lawson |accessdate=March 9, 2014 |work=IAAF}}</ref> She competed in the [[2014 IAAF World Indoor Championships – Women's 60 metres|60 metres event]] at the [[2014 IAAF World Indoor Championships]].<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.teamusa.org/usa-track-and-field/athletes/Lekeisha-Lawson  |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20151208041915/http://www.teamusa.org/usa-track-and-field/athletes/Lekeisha-Lawson  |url-status=dead  |archive-date=December 8, 2015  |title=LaKeisha Lawson Team USA Track and Field profile |accessdate=November 28, 2015 |work=Team USA}}</ref>

==Professional career==
Coach Lekeisha Moore enters was named the head coach at [[Cal State Dominguez Hills Toros]] in 2024.

After spending three seasons (2021 - 2024) as the track and field assistant coach with [[Claremont-Mudd-Scripps Stags and Athenas]]. Moore was named the [[U.S. Track & Field and Cross Country Coaches Association]] Men's Track and Field West Region Assistant Coach of the Year in 2023, after having a key role in the performance of the CMS sprinters.

In particular, Christian Campbell was the SCIAC Track Athlete of the Year after setting [[Southern California Intercollegiate Athletic Conference]] records in the 100 and 200 meters, breaking CMS standards that had stood for 35 years. The Stags also broke school records in the 4x100 and 4x400 relays, with the 4x400 team recording the fourth-fastest time in Division III history at the [[NCAA Division III]] Championships to earn second place .

Moore graduated from the [[University of Nevada-Las Vegas]] with a degree in journalism in 2009 and is a native of [[Victorville, California]]. Her husband, Carlos Moore, is a former World and National Junior Championship sprinter for [[USA Track and Field]].

Moore coached with CYP Training and helped put multiple high school athletes in state meets, as well as contributing to scholarships earned by most of the athletes involved in the CYP sprint group over her six seasons. She also served as the head coach at Glendora and Bonita High Schools, coaching top sprint teams through CIF Championships.<ref>[https://goccaa.org/news/2024/7/30/womens-track-and-field-csudh-athletics-welcomes-lekeisha-moore-as-new-track-field-head-coach.aspx CSUDH Athletics Welcomes Lekeisha Moore As New Track & Field Head Coach] [[California Collegiate Athletic Association]]</ref>

'''Danilo Teodoro Soares''' (born 29 October 1991) is a Brazilian professional [[association football|footballer]] who plays as a [[left back]] for [[Austrian Football Bundesliga|Austrian Bundesliga]] club [[SC Austria Lustenau|Austria Lustenau]].

Born in [[Belo Horizonte]], Brazil, Soares started his career in Austria with [[SC Austria Lustenau|Austria Lustenau]] in 2010. He joined [[FC Ingolstadt 04|FC Ingolstadt]] of the [[2. Bundesliga]] in summer 2013 and was promoted to the Bundesliga with the club in 2015, but injury issues limited him to just a single Bundesliga appearance and his left the club at the end of the season. He spent the 2016–17 season with [[TSG 1899 Hoffenheim|TSG Hoffenheim]] but failed to make an appearance, with Soares joining [[VfL Bochum]] in summer 2017. He was promoted to the Bundesliga with Bochum at the end of the [[2020–21 VfL Bochum season|2020–21 season]].

==Career==
===Austria Lustenau===
Born in [[Belo Horizonte]],<ref name="auto10" /> Soares went to schools in the [[Venda Nova, Belo Horizonte|Venda Nova]] neighbourhood of Belo Horizonte.<ref name="auto2">{{Cite web |last=Bianchini |first=Vladimir |date=28 August 2020 |title=Ídolo na Alemanha, ele venceu a depressão e revela seu grande sonho: 'Jogar no Atlético-MG' |url=https://www.espn.com.br/historias-da-bola/artigo/_/id/7344974/bundesliga-danilo-soares-depressao-e-revela-sonho-jogar-no-atletico-mg |access-date=22 September 2021 |website=ESPN.com |language=pt}}</ref> His parents separated when he was a child and he experienced depression as a result.<ref name="auto2" /> Having previously had an unsuccessful trial at [[Cruzeiro Esporte Clube|Cruzeiro]] at around age 16, he spent a month on trial in the Netherlands, before signing a three-year contract with Austrian [[Austrian Football First League|First League]] (second tier) club [[SC Austria Lustenau|Austria Lustenau]] in 2010.<ref name="auto2" /><ref>{{Cite interview |last=Soares |first=Danilo |interviewer=Claudio Gentile |title=Der Mann auf hinten links – ein Interview mit Danilo Soares |url=https://einsachtvieracht.de/2020/10/30/der-mann-auf-hinten-links-ein-interview-mit-danilo-soares/ |access-date=22 September 2021 |work=einsachtvieracht.de |date=30 October 2020 |language=de}}</ref> He made 26 appearances during the [[2010–11 Austrian Football First League|2010–11 season]], 34 appearances in the [[2011–12 Austrian Football First League|2011–12 season]], and 31 appearances during the [[2012–13 Austrian Football First League|2012–13 season]], scoring once.<ref name="wf2">{{Cite web |title=Danilo Soares » Club matches |url=https://www.worldfootball.net/person/pe223293/danilo-soares/club-matches/ |access-date=22 September 2021 |website=worldfootball.net}}</ref>

===FC Ingolstadt===
In summer 2013, Soares joined [[FC Ingolstadt 04|FC Ingolstadt]], having signed a pre-contract agreement during the previous season.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Adam |first=Christian |date=16 January 2013 |title=Soares wechselt nach Ingolstadt |url=https://www.vn.at/sport/2013/01/16/soares-wechselt-nach-ingolstadt.vn |access-date=22 September 2021 |website=Vorarlberger Nachrichten |language=de}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |date=27 March 2013 |title=FCI-Planungsstand: Metzelder vor Abschied |url=https://www.kicker.de/fci-planungsstand_metzelder-vor-abschied-583860/artikel |access-date=22 September 2021 |website=kicker |language=de}}</ref> He made his debut for the club on 19 July 2013, starting in a 2–1 [[2. Bundesliga]] defeat at home to [[FC Erzgebirge Aue]].<ref name="kicker1314">{{Cite web |title=Danilo Soares {{pipe}} FC Ingolstadt 04 {{pipe}} 2. Bundesliga {{pipe}} 2013/14 {{pipe}} Spielerprofil |url=https://www.kicker.de/danilo-soares/spieler/2-bundesliga/2013-14/fc-ingolstadt-04 |access-date=22 September 2021 |website=kicker |language=de}}</ref> He made 27 league appearances and two [[DFB-Pokal]] appearances across the [[2013–14 FC Ingolstadt 04 season|2013–14 season]].<ref name="kicker1314" /> On 2 March 2015, Soares scored his first goal for the club in a 1–1 draw with [[TSV 1860 Munich|1860 Munich]].<ref name="auto1">{{Cite web |date=2 March 2015 |title=Derby gegen die Löwen: FC04 kommt über ein 1:1 nicht hinaus |url=https://www.donaukurier.de/sport/fussball/fcingolstadt04/fc04-berichte/FC-Ingolstadt-04-aufmacher-dkonline_PMG-0815-Derby-gegen-die-Loewen-FC04-kommt-ueber-ein-1-1-nicht-hinaus;art19158,3023867 |access-date=22 September 2021 |website=Donaukurier |language=de }}{{Dead link|date=August 2025 |bot=InternetArchiveBot |fix-attempted=yes }}</ref> Despite suffering an injury in his left foot in early April, he appeared in 6 of 8 matches across April and May 2015, as Ingolstadt pushed for promotion.<ref name="auto1" /> The [[2014–15 FC Ingolstadt 04 season|2014–15 season]] saw Ingolstadt promoted to the [[Bundesliga]] as champions of the 2. Bundesliga with 64 points.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Tabelle {{pipe}} 34. Spieltag {{pipe}} 2. Bundesliga 2014/15 |url=https://www.kicker.de/2-bundesliga/tabelle/2014-15 |access-date=22 September 2021 |website=kicker |language=de}}</ref> Soares started 32 of the club's 34 league matches that season, and scored once.<ref name="kicker1415">{{Cite web |title=Danilo Soares {{pipe}} FC Ingolstadt 04 {{pipe}} 2. Bundesliga {{pipe}} 2014/15 {{pipe}} Spielerprofil |url=https://www.kicker.de/danilo-soares/spieler/2-bundesliga/2014-15/fc-ingolstadt-04 |access-date=22 September 2021 |website=kicker |language=de}}</ref> Following the end of the season, he had surgery on his [[metatarsophalangeal joint]], ruling him out for an extended period of time.<ref>{{Cite web |date=24 June 2015 |title=Danilo fällt längere Zeit aus |url=https://www.donaukurier.de/sport/fussball/fcingolstadt04/fc04-berichte/Schanzer-FC-Ingolstadt-Danilo-Soares-Ingolstadt-Danilo-faellt-laengere-Zeit-aus;art19158,3068409 |access-date=22 September 2021 |website=Donaukurier |language=de}}</ref> Having returned from injury, Soares made his first Bundesliga appearance on 19 December 2015 in a 1–0 defeat to [[Bayer 04 Leverkusen|Bayer Leverkusen]], and he committed to seeing out the season with Ingolstadt in January 2021.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Sterner |first=Gottfried |date=4 January 2016 |title=Ingolstadt: Personalkarussell beim FC Ingolstadt kommt langsam in Bewegung |url=https://www.donaukurier.de/sport/fussball/fcingolstadt04/fc04-berichte/Ingolstadt-wochennl012016-Pekhart-erhaelt-Freigabe-Danilo-will-bleiben;art19158,3165260 |access-date=22 September 2021 |website=Donaukurier |language=de |archive-date=29 November 2018 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20181129021822/https://www.donaukurier.de/sport/fussball/fcingolstadt04/fc04-berichte/Ingolstadt-wochennl012016-Pekhart-erhaelt-Freigabe-Danilo-will-bleiben;art19158,3165260 |url-status=dead }}</ref> However, he did not make a further appearance during the [[2015–16 FC Ingolstadt 04 season|2015–16 season]], and was released at the end of the season, with Soares continuing to suffer injury to his left toe, including the onset of [[osteoarthritis]].<ref name="auto3">{{Cite web |title=Danilo Soares {{pipe}} FC Ingolstadt 04 {{pipe}} Bundesliga {{pipe}} 2015/16 {{pipe}} Spielerprofil |url=https://www.kicker.de/danilo-soares/spieler/bundesliga/2015-16/fc-ingolstadt-04 |access-date=22 September 2021 |website=kicker |language=de}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last1=Pfeifer |first1=Michael |last2=Kaiser |first2=Harald |date=27 April 2016 |title=Hoffenheim hat Danilo weiter auf dem Zettel ===1899 Hoffenheim===

'''Giselle Loren "Gigi" Lazzarato'''<ref>{{Cite web |last=Gorgeous |first=Gigi |date=November 29, 2015 |title=SNAPCHAT Q&A: My Real Name, Being Single & More {{!}} Gigi |url=https://m.youtube.com/watch?v=4Qr1BjZhnpg&t=85s&pp=2AFfkAIB |access-date=July 3, 2025 |website=Youtube}}</ref> (born April 20, 1992), formerly '''Getty''', known professionally as '''Gigi Gorgeous''',<ref name=TC200114>{{cite web| url = https://www.townandcountrymag.com/society/tradition/a30361901/ariadne-natalia-august-getty-gigi-gorgeous-family-interview/| title = Outrageous Fortune: Nats, August, and Gigi Gorgeous Getty Are Not Your Typical Old-Money Scions| last = Reginato| first = James| date = January 14, 2020| website = [[Town & Country (magazine)|Town & Country]]| publisher = Hearst| access-date = February 15, 2021| archive-date = October 31, 2020| archive-url = https://web.archive.org/web/20201031161711/https://www.townandcountrymag.com/society/tradition/a30361901/ariadne-natalia-august-getty-gigi-gorgeous-family-interview/| url-status = live}}</ref> is a Canadian [[List of YouTubers|YouTuber]], socialite, actress, and model.

In 2008, Lazzarato began uploading [[video blog]]s onto streaming platform YouTube.<ref name=DB130123/> Her videos achieved popularity and established an [[Fan base|online following]]. During the following years, Lazzarato uploaded regularly to the channel along with creating and starring in the [[reality program]] ''[[The Avenue (web series)|The Avenue]]'' (2011–2013). Following a brief hiatus, she gained media attention after [[coming out]] as a [[transgender woman]] in 2013, and began going by Gigi Gorgeous.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.realself.com/forum/gender-reassignment-surgery-gigi-gorgeous-shares-story-female-video |title=Gender Reassignment Surgery: Gigi Gorgeous Shares Her Story "I Want To Be Female" -Video – MTF Breast Augmentation forum |publisher=Realself.com |date=March 9, 2015 |access-date=May 20, 2015 |archive-date=May 31, 2019 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190531142240/https://www.realself.com/forum/gender-reassignment-surgery-gigi-gorgeous-shares-story-female-video |url-status=live }}</ref><ref>{{cite web |last=Klee |first=Miles |url=http://www.dailydot.com/entertainment/gigi-gorgeous-lgbt-wcw/ |title=How WCW Gigi Gorgeous has changed the trans community for the better |publisher=Dailydot.com |date=May 6, 2015 |access-date=May 20, 2015 |archive-date=March 4, 2016 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160304223748/http://www.dailydot.com/entertainment/gigi-gorgeous-lgbt-wcw/ |url-status=live }}</ref> During 2014, Lazzarato personally documented her gender transition through social media profiles, notably through videos revolving around cosmetic procedures, which obtained [[Viral video|viral status]]. In 2016, an incident involving Lazzarato being deported from [[Dubai]] due to her status as a transgender woman resulted in widespread media coverage. Lazzarato was the subject of ''This is Everything: Gigi Gorgeous'' (2017), a [[Barbara Kopple]]-directed documentary that followed life going through gender transition. The film premiered at the [[Sundance Film Festival]] and went on to have a limited theatrical release and several accolades including a [[Streamy]].

Besides personality work, Lazzarato has dabbled in acting and [[Fashion model|modeling]] work. Her performance credits include starring in fellow YouTuber [[Shane Dawson]]'s short film ''I Hate Myselfie'' (2015) and its sequel, along with guest appearances in television series ''[[Project Runway All Stars]]'', ''[[Me and My Grandma]]'', ''[[Good Work (talk show)|Good Work]]'', and ''Trailblazers'', amongst others. Through modeling, Lazzarato has appeared on the covers of ''[[Paper (magazine)|Paper]]'' and ''[[Fashion (magazine)|Fashion]]'', been featured in spreads for ''Galore'', ''Kode'', ''[[Refinery29]]'', and ''[[Out (magazine)|Out]]'' and served as a frequent muse of [[August Getty Atelier]]. In 2019, she authored the book ''He Said, She Said: Lessons, Stories, and Mistakes From My Transgender Journey''.

=== 2014–16: Gender transition and appearances ===
Lazzarato was awarded the [[LogoTV]] Trailblazing Social Creator Award in 2014 for being an advocate on behalf of [[LGBT]] youth. ==== 2016: Dubai incident ====
On August 9, 2016, Lazzarato was detained in the [[United Arab Emirates]]. Her passport was taken by airport officials and immigration officers at the [[Dubai International Airport]]. She was denied entry to [[Dubai]] for "imitation of women by men", despite the fact that, as confirmed by Lazzarato, "the gender on [her] passport states female and not male." The "imitation of women by men" is [[LGBT rights in the United Arab Emirates|illegal in the UAE]], and violators can face up to a year in jail.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.pride.com/transgender/2016/8/10/dubai-airport-officials-detained-gigi-gorgeous-because-shes-trans|title=Dubai Airport Officials Detained Gigi Gorgeous Because She's Trans|date=August 10, 2016|access-date=August 10, 2016|archive-date=August 11, 2016|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160811162437/http://www.pride.com/transgender/2016/8/10/dubai-airport-officials-detained-gigi-gorgeous-because-shes-trans|url-status=live}}</ref> She was released after being detained for five hours.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.mtv.com/news/2917222/gigi-gorgeous-dubai/|title=Gigi Gorgeous Was Held In A Dubai Airport For Being Transgender|website=[[MTV]]|access-date=August 10, 2016|archive-date=August 11, 2016|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160811001843/http://www.mtv.com/news/2917222/gigi-gorgeous-dubai/|url-status=dead}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.people.com/article/gigi-gorgeous-detained-dubai-airport-transgender|title=Model Gigi Gorgeous Detained at Dubai Airport for Being Transgender: 'One of the Scariest Moments of My Life'|access-date=August 10, 2016|archive-date=August 11, 2016|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160811070219/http://www.people.com/article/gigi-gorgeous-detained-dubai-airport-transgender|url-status=live}}</ref>

The "#JusticeForGigi" hashtag surfaced on Twitter, with fans and supporters calling for her release and a reform in anti-LGBTQ laws.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://twitter.com/hashtag/JusticeForGigi?src=hash|title=#JusticeForGigi hashtag on Twitter|access-date=August 10, 2016|archive-date=May 9, 2020|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200509010140/https://twitter.com/hashtag/JusticeForGigi?src=hash|url-status=live}}</ref> It was not the first time a transgender person had been detained in Dubai. In 2014, two Brazilian transgender women were also detained and had their passports taken.<ref>{{cite web |last1=Sieczkowski |first1=Cavan |date=August 10, 2016 |title=YouTube Star Was Allegedly Detained In Dubai Airport Because She's Trans |url=https://huffingtonpost.com/entry/gigi-gorgeous-dubai-airport-transgender_us_57ab2f3be4b06e52746e78cf |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170310011016/http://www.huffingtonpost.com/entry/gigi-gorgeous-dubai-airport-transgender_us_57ab2f3be4b06e52746e78cf |archive-date=March 10, 2017 |access-date=December 12, 2019 |website=[[HuffPost]]}}</ref> Before leaving Dubai for Sweden, Lazzarato responded to the incident by calling for equality and legal protections for LGBTQ people.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.usmagazine.com/celebrity-news/news/gigi-gorgeous-detained-in-dubai-for-being-transgender-w433698|title=Gigi Gorgeous Detained in Dubai for Being Transgender |work=[[Us Weekly]] |date=August 10, 2016|access-date=August 10, 2016|archive-date=August 10, 2016|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160810214051/http://www.usmagazine.com/celebrity-news/news/gigi-gorgeous-detained-in-dubai-for-being-transgender-w433698|url-status=live}}</ref>

In June 2017, Lazzarato was named to the ''[[Time (magazine)|Time]]'' magazine list of the 25 most influential people on the Internet.<ref name="time-26jun2017">{{cite magazine|title=The 25 Most Influential People on the Internet|url=https://time.com/4815217/most-influential-people-internet/|access-date=June 27, 2017|magazine=[[Time (magazine)|Time]]|date=June 26, 2017|archive-date=May 18, 2019|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190518224033/http://time.com/4815217/most-influential-people-internet/|url-status=live}}</ref>

=== Transition ===
Lazzarato came out as a [[transgender woman]] in December 2013. On March 8, 2014, she legally changed her name to Gigi Loren Lazzarato.<ref name="files.ontario.ca">{{Cite news|date=March 8, 2014|title=The Ontario Gazette|journal=The Ontario Gazette = Gazette de l'Ontario|language=en|volume=147–10|page=572|publisher=Ministry of Government Services|agency=Queen's Printer for Ontario|url=https://files.ontario.ca/gazette_docs/gazette_march_8_ont06_028206.pdf|access-date=February 11, 2021|issn=0030-2937|archive-date=March 2, 2016|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160302230158/https://files.ontario.ca/gazette_docs/gazette_march_8_ont06_028206.pdf|url-status=live}}</ref>

In a September 2015 issue of ''[[People (magazine)|People]]'', Lazzarato credited "transgender model and performing artist [[Amanda Lepore]] and the death of my mother for sparking my transition."<ref>{{cite web|title=Transgender YouTube Star Gigi Gorgeous: How My Mom's Death Inspired Me to Transition|url=http://www.people.com/article/gigi-gorgeous-youtube-transition-mothers-death|website=[[People (magazine)|People]] |access-date=April 14, 2016|archive-date=April 20, 2016|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160420222018/http://www.people.com/article/gigi-gorgeous-youtube-transition-mothers-death|url-status=live}}</ref>
