{{Nihongo|'''Chinami Hashimoto'''|橋本 ちなみ|Hashimoto Chinami|born July 17, 1992}}<ref>{{cite episode|title=Imocho Radio|series=[[Recently, My Sister Is Unusual]]|network=Hibiki Radio Station|date=January 30, 2014}}</ref> is a Japanese [[Voice acting in Japan|voice actress]] from [[Nagano Prefecture]] affiliated with VIMS.

==Biography==
Hashimoto became interested in acting, while watching a concert held by the cast for the anime series ''[[Di Gi Charat]]''. Although her parents were disapproved of her plans, partly as a joke, she enrolled at a voice acting school operated by the agency VIMS.<ref name="seigura201404">{{Cite journal|journal=Seiyū Grand Prix|issue=April 2015|title=New Voice Actor Notebook|first=Yoshikatsu|last=Nakagami|page=11|date=March 10, 2014}}</ref> She made her voice acting debut as Mitsuki Kanzaki, the lead character of the 2014 anime television series ''[[Recently, My Sister Is Unusual]]''.<ref name="imocho">{{cite web|first=Lynzee|last=Loveridge|title=Chinami Hashimoto, Junji Majima Star in Saikin, Imōto no Yōsu ga Chotto Okashiin Da Ga Anime|url=http://www.animenewsnetwork.com/news/2013-11-09/chinami-hashimoto-junji-majima-star-in-saikin-imoto-no-yosu-ga-chotto-okaishiin-da-ga-anime|website=[[Anime News Network]]|date=November 9, 2013|access-date=December 1, 2015}}</ref>

'''Woody Goss''' (born c. 1989)<ref name="wg-umich-no label" /> is an American musician, keyboardist and songwriter. He is best known as a founding member of the funk band [[Vulfpeck]]. His background spans several genres including [[funk]], [[jazz]], [[R&B]], and [[pop music|pop]]. He has released several solo albums, and albums in collaboration with Jeremy Daly and [[May Erlewine]]. His most recent album ''High Loon!'' was released in 2023.

==Life and career==
[[File:Cory Wong-with Vulfpeck-at-crystal-ballroom-may-26-2017 (cropped).jpg|thumb|Goss (right) performing with [[Vulfpeck]] in 2017.]]
Goss grew up in [[Skokie, Illinois]]. His father had a passion for [[jazz]] music and played the piano. Goss started to play piano at age seven. In his early teens he was drawn to [[bebop jazz]] through the works of pianist [[Thelonious Monk]]. In high school he was drawn to [[funk]] music through the works of [[George Clinton (funk musician)|George Clinton]], [[Sly and the Family Stone]] and [[James Brown]]. He played in the rhythm section of his high school band.<ref name="wg-third story-2019" /><ref name="wg-medium-2015" />

He studied jazz piano at the [[University of Michigan School of Music]]. In college he played [[psychedelic jazz]] in a band called Honey. He booked musical acts at the Canterbury House, a church and music venue associated with the university. The venue became a hub where Goss met like-minded musicians, including [[Jack Stratton (musician)|Jack Stratton]] and [[Theo Katzman]], who along with Goss and bassist [[Joe Dart]] started recording as [[Vulfpeck]] in 2011.<ref name="wg-third story-2019" /><ref name="wg-medium-2015" /><ref name="wg-canterbury" />

Goss has recorded six albums and four extended plays with Vulfpeck. His songwriting credits with the band include "Tee Time", "Fugue State", "Dean Town", "My First Car", "A Walk to Remember" and others.<ref name="wg-medium-2015" /><ref name="wg-live-oct2016" /><ref name="wg-dart clinic-2018" /><ref name="wg-tee time-2017" /> In 2019, he released a Christmas album titled ''A Very Vulfy Christmas'' consisting of eight jazz-style rearrangements of Vulfpeck originals. The recordings feature drummer [[Dana Hall (musician)|Dana Hall]] and bassists Matt Ulery and Joe Fee. The album was accompanied by a [[Peanuts|''Peanuts''-style]] cartoon of the same title, written by Goss and Sean Peecook, and featuring the members of Vulfpeck as cartoon characters.<ref name="wg-third story-2019" /><ref name="wg-christmas-dec2019" />

Goss has released two jazz albums and one R&B album as a solo artist, titled ''Solo Rhodes'' (2016), ''Rainbow Beach'' (2021), and ''High Loon!'' (2023).<ref name="wg-solo albums" /><ref name="wg-chirp-2022" />{{efn|name=genre}} He has released three albums in collaboration with musician Jeremy Daly titled ''Strange Satisfaction'' (2020), ''Gravy in My Coffee'' (2021), and ''Hold Up, Look Back'' (2024).<ref name="wg-woody and jeremy" /> The albums are categorized on streaming services as pop, rock, and alternative.{{efn|name=genre}} In 2020, Goss and singer-songwriter [[May Erlewine]] jointly produced and released an album titled ''Anyway''.<ref name="wg-anyway-2020" />

==Influences==
Goss started with classical piano lessons at an early age.<ref name="wg-allegra-interview" /> His interest and musical influences evolved over time from oldies R&B-pop as a child, to [[bebop jazz]] via [[Thelonious Monk]] as a teenager, to [[funk]] and groove-based music via [[Parliament-Funkadelic]] and [[James Brown]] in high school, to [[experimental rock]] via [[Frank Zappa]] and [[Ween]] in college.<ref name="wg-third story-2019" /><ref name="wg-medium-2015" /> His bandmates Stratton and Dart describe him as a natural improviser.<ref name="wg-medium-2015" /><ref name="wg-dart clinic-2018" />

==Personal life==
Goss is an avid [[Birdwatching|birdwatcher]] and lives in the Chicago area.<ref name="wg-chirp-2022" /><ref name="wg-chicago bird" /> He has led workshops and master classes at the Music Department of [[Columbia College Chicago]].<ref name="wg-columbia" />

'''Nolan Blake Garrett''' (September 14, 1992 – February 8, 2026) was an American film and stage actor, best known for his role as Plug in the children's [[Comedy film|comedy]] film ''[[How to Eat Fried Worms (film)|How to Eat Fried Worms]]''.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Staff |first=T. M. Z. |date=February 9, 2026 |title=Blake Garrett, Child Actor in 'How to Eat Fried Worms,' Dead at 33 |url=https://www.tmz.com/2026/02/09/blake-garrett-dead/ |access-date=February 14, 2026 |website=TMZ |language=en}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |date=February 9, 2026 |title=Blake Garrett, Former Child Actor From How to Eat Fried Worms, Dead at 33 |url=https://www.eonline.com/news/1428388/blake-garrett-how-to-eat-friend-worms-child-actor-dead-at-33 |access-date=February 14, 2026 |website=E! Online|last=Rahbar|first=Sabba}}</ref>

== Life and career ==
Even at a young age, Garrett showed an interest in acting and the performing arts, which led him to begin his artistic career in local theatre productions at a young age.<ref>{{Cite web |date=February 10, 2026 |title=Blake Garrett, Child Actor, Dies at 33 |url=https://www.chosun.com/english/kpop-culture-en/2026/02/10/VMN27F2PXRGLFHBMXSY3RBMFWY/ |access-date=February 14, 2026 |website=The Chosun Daily |language=en}}</ref>

From an early age, he dedicated himself to acting and appeared in local theatre productions such as ''Aladdin and His Magic Lamp'', ''Peanuts: A Charlie Brown Tribute'', ''[[The Wizard of Oz (2011 musical)|The Wizard of Oz]]'', ''[[Annie (musical)|Annie]]'' and ''[[Grease (musical)|Grease]]''. At the age of ten, he joined the international tour of ''[[Barney's Colorful World]]'' and performed roles in the live show.<ref>{{Cite web |date=February 9, 2026 |title=Blake Garrett, Child Actor in 'How to Eat Fried Worms,' Dead at 33 |url=https://www.foxbangor.com/news/national/entertainment/blake-garrett-child-actor-in-how-to-eat-fried-worms-dead-at-33/article_ae9083a3-a389-5ccd-9d84-ddde92f2c4f9.html |access-date=February 14, 2026 |website=FOX 22/ABC 7 |language=en}}</ref><ref>{{Cite news |last=Reiher |first=Andrea |date=February 9, 2026 |title=Former Child Star Dead at 33 After Sudden Medical Emergency |url=https://parade.com/news/blake-garrett-dead-how-to-eat-fried-worms-child-actor |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20260211010850/https://parade.com/news/blake-garrett-dead-how-to-eat-fried-worms-child-actor |archive-date=February 11, 2026 |access-date=February 14, 2026 |work=Parade |language=en|url-status=live}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=Taylor |first=Adam |date=February 10, 2026 |title=Former Child Star Dies at 33: RIP Blake Garrett |url=https://www.wideopencountry.com/former-child-star-dies-at-33-rip-blake-garrett/ |access-date=February 14, 2026 |website=Wide Open Country |language=en-US}}</ref>

Garrett's best-known film role was in the 2006 family comedy ''[[How to Eat Fried Worms (film)|How to Eat Fried Worms]]'', based on the children's book of the same name. He played Plug, a classmate of the protagonist. His performance was part of the ensemble cast that won the award for Best Child Ensemble in a Feature Film at the [[28th Young Artist Awards|2007 Young Artist Awards]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=Blake Garrett, child actor from 'How to Eat Fried Worms,' dies at 33 |url=https://ew.com/blake-garrett-dead-how-to-eat-fried-worms-child-actor-was-33-11903162 |access-date=February 14, 2026 |website=EW.com |language=en|date=February 9, 2026|last=Shewfelt|first=Raechal}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=Sharma |first=Isha |date=February 9, 2026 |title=Former Child Star Suddenly Passes Away at 33: Our Hearts Go Out to His Family |url=https://entertainmentnow.com/news/blake-garrett-child-actor-passes-away-tributes/ |access-date=February 14, 2026 |website=EntertainmentNow |language=en-US}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |title=29th Annual Young Artist Awards - Nominations / Special Awards |url=http://www.youngartistawards.org/noms29.html |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20080706161000/http://www.youngartistawards.org/noms29.html |archive-date=July 6, 2008 |access-date=February 14, 2026 |website=www.youngartistawards.org|url-status=dead}}</ref>

After his time as a child actor, Garrett led a relatively private life. He struggled with addiction and managed to remain sober in the years leading up to his death. He lived in [[Tulsa, Oklahoma|Tulsa]] in his later years.<ref>{{Cite web |date=February 10, 2026 |title=Former Child Star Blake Garrett Dies at 33 |url=https://www.complex.com/pop-culture/a/bernadette-giacomazzo/blake-garrett-how-to-eat-fried-worms-dead |access-date=February 14, 2026 |website=Complex |language=en|last=Giacomazzo|first=Bernadette}}</ref><ref>{{Cite news |title=Former Child Actor Blake Garrett from 'How to Eat Fried Worms' Dies at 33 |url=https://people.com/how-to-eat-fried-worms-child-actor-blake-garrett-dead-33-11902984 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20260210092624/https://people.com/how-to-eat-fried-worms-child-actor-blake-garrett-dead-33-11902984 |archive-date=February 10, 2026 |access-date=February 14, 2026 |work=People.com|url-status=live}}</ref> 

In February 2026 Garrett was brought to the emergency room in extreme pain, which was later determined to be [[shingles]]. He died on February 8, 2026, at the age of 33. In an interview with [[TMZ]], Garrett's mother stated that she believed he may have self-medicated to cope with the pain, and that they were awaiting an autopsy to determine the cause of death.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Moorman |first=Taijuan |title='How to Eat Fried Worms' child star Blake Garrett dies at 33 in Oklahoma |url=https://www.oklahoman.com/story/entertainment/2026/02/10/blake-garrett-dead-how-to-eat-fried-worms-actor-oklahoma/88603974007/ |access-date=February 14, 2026 |website=The Oklahoman |language=en-US|date=February 10, 2026|last2=Derksen|first2=Cheyenne}}</ref><ref name="TMZ">{{Cite web |date=2026-02-09 |title=Blake Garrett, Child Actor in 'How to Eat Fried Worms,' Dead at 33 |url=https://www.tmz.com/2026/02/09/blake-garrett-dead/ |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20260215140125/https://www.tmz.com/2026/02/09/blake-garrett-dead/ |archive-date=2026-02-15 |access-date=2026-02-22 |website=TMZ |language=en}}</ref> In July, it was determined Garrett died from an accidental [[fentanyl]] overdose.<ref>[https://deadline.com/2026/07/blake-garrett-cause-of-death-former-child-actor-1236981450/ Blake Garrett Cause Of Death Revealed]</ref>

'''James Anthony Janisse''' (born May 6, 1989), is an American [[YouTuber]], filmmaker, writer, editor, executive producer, and actor. He is best known as the founder and host of the YouTube channel [[Dead Meat (YouTube channel)|Dead Meat]], which features the popular series ''[[The Kill Count (webshow)|The Kill Count]]'', horror podcasts, and interviews. 

Janisse has appeared in several film and television productions, including ''[[In Search of Darkness]]'' (2019), ''[[Scream (2022 film)|Scream]]'' (2022), ''Friendsgiving'' (2023),  ''[[Little Bites]]'' (2024), and ''[[Hysteria!]]'' (2024). He also appeared in the second season of the web series ''The Look-See'' (2018) and directed ''[[Fresh Meat (2026 film)|Fresh Meat]]'' (2026).

== Early life ==
James Anthony Janisse was born on May 6, 1989, in [[Detroit, Michigan]]. He developed a passion for horror films at a young age, citing [[Scream (franchise)|''Scream'' franchise]] as his introduction to the genre. As a child, he learned [[HTML]] to create a website dedicated to counting kills in horror movies.<ref name="DM">{{cite web|title=James A. Janisse – Bio|url=https://deadmeat.rip/team-member/james-a-janisse/|website=[[Dead Meat (YouTube channel)|Dead Meat]]|access-date=February 20, 2026}}</ref> Janisse earned a degree in [[Bachelor of Film and Television|filmmaking]] from the [[University of Michigan]].<ref>{{Cite news |date=2021-04-26 |title=Meet James A. Janisse: Host & Media Commentator |url=https://shoutoutla.com/meet-james-a-janisse-host-media-commentator/ |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220311142735/https://shoutoutla.com/meet-james-a-janisse-host-media-commentator/ |archive-date=2022-03-11 |access-date=2026-02-20 |work=Shoutout LA |language=en-US}}</ref>

== Career ==
===2009–2016: Early career===
Before Janisse became a content creator on [[YouTube]], he worked as an actor and appeared in 2009 short film ''Everyone's a V.I.P. to Someone'' in a small role.<ref name="avmedia">{{cite AV media notes|title=Everyone's a V.I.P. to Someone|others=Paolo Carone, Chelsea Leonowicz|publisher=Independent Film Press|type=2009}}</ref> Janisse spent over five years co-running comedy YouTube channels with his now-wife [[Chelsea Rebecca]], starting with Comediocracy and later Practical Folks in 2010.<ref name="HR1">{{cite web|title=Meet YouTube's Impresario of Horror: James A. Janisse|url=https://www.hollywoodreporter.com/business/digital/youtube-impresario-horror-james-a-janisse-dead-meat-1235302291/|website=[[The Hollywood Reporter]]|access-date=February 20, 2026|last=Bonilla|first=Justina}}</ref> While studying at the University of Michigan, he began making comedy videos together with Rebecca.<ref name=Paste>{{cite web |last=Mitchell |first=Matt |title=YouTube Channel Dead Meat Gives Hilarious New Life to Horror Film Legacies |url=https://www.pastemagazine.com/comedy/dead-meat-interview |website=[[Paste (magazine)|Paste Magazine]] |date=June 14, 2022 |access-date=February 20, 2026}}</ref>

In 2011, they founded Comediocracy, which was later removed by YouTube, and then launched Practical Folks with James Graessle and Joel Arnold.<ref name="Paste" /> Handling most of the editing for Practical Folks limited his creative freedom, so he left the channel and spent late 2016 to early 2017 developing a new horror-focused project, [[Dead Meat (YouTube channel)|Dead Meat]].<ref name=Paste/>

=== 2017–present: Dead Meat ===
{{Main|Dead Meat (YouTube channel)}}
Janisse launched Dead Meat in 2017 with its flagship show ''[[The Kill Count (webshow)|The Kill Count]]'', where he breaks down horror movies, highlights memorable deaths, shares trivia, and notes production details. The channel grew fast, and by 2022 it had 5.94 million subscribers and more than 2 billion views.<ref name="HR1" /> He is president and executive producer of Dead Meat, which he co-owns with Rebecca, who launched the [[Dead Meat Podcast]] in 2018.<ref name="HR1" />

In 2018, Janisse appeared in the second season of [[Crypt TV]]'s ''The Look-See'', where he played the role of Raymond.<ref name="deadline">{{Cite web |last=Hipes |first=Patrick |date=2018-07-18 |title=Crypt TV’s ‘The Look-See’ To Get Season 2 Premiere Screening At RTX Austin |url=https://deadline.com/2018/07/crypt-tv-the-look-see-renewed-season-2-1202401974/ |access-date=2026-02-21 |website=[[Deadline Hollywood|Deadline]] |language=en-US}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=Weiss |first=Geoff |date=2018-06-04 |title=Crypt TV Casts Horror YouTuber James ‘Deadmeat’ Janisse For Season Two Of 'The Look-See' |url=https://www.tubefilter.com/2018/06/04/crypt-tv-james-deadmeat-janisse-the-look-see/ |access-date=2026-02-22 |website=[[Tubefilter]] |language=en-US}}</ref> In 2022, streaming service [[Shudder (streaming service)|Shudder]] sponsored the [[Dead Meat Horror Awards]]. Winners, chosen by him and his wife, were presented by their friends from the horror community.<ref name="MovieWeb">{{cite web |last=Bolton |first=Cameron |title=Dead Meat Creator Addresses the Massive Popularity of Horror Movies |url=https://movieweb.com/dead-meat-owners/ |website=[[MovieWeb]] |date=January 24, 2023 |access-date=February 20, 2026}}</ref> He has also appeared in acting roles, such as playing Toby, a store clerk in the Thanksgiving horror-comedy ''Fiendsgiving'' alongside [[Samm Levine]].<ref name="Fang">{{cite web|title=Exclusive: Dead Meat's James A. Janisse Joins Clarke Wolfe's Thanksgiving Slasher Fiendsgiving|url=https://www.fangoria.com/exclusives-fiendsgiving-casting-news/|website=[[Fangoria]]|access-date=February 20, 2026|last=T|first=Amber}}</ref> He has expressed interest in professional wrestling and has begun training for a potential future match.<ref name="Fight">{{cite web|title=Dead Meat's James A. Janisse Teases Possible Wrestling Debut, Says It’s A Bucket List Item For Him|url=https://www.fightful.com/wrestling/dead-meat-s-james-janisse-teases-possible-wrestling-debut-says-it-s-bucket-list-item-him/|website=Fightful|access-date=February 20, 2026}}</ref> He has explained that his on-camera persona in ''The Kill Count'' is partly a character, while he is more candid on the podcast.<ref name="DD" /> His favorite films include [[John Carpenter]]'s ''[[The Thing (1982 film)|The Thing]]'' and ''[[Scream (1996 film)|Scream]]'' (1996).<ref name="DD">{{cite web|title=A Bloody Dead Meat Christmas Interview with James A. Janisse, Chelsea Rebecca, and Wim Sweldens|url=https://dailydead.com/a-bloody-dead-meat-christmas-interview-with-james-a-janisse-chelsea-rebecca-and-wim-sweldens/|website=Daily Dead|access-date=February 20, 2026}}</ref><ref>{{Cite book |last=Pettis |first=Caillou |title=The Inspiring World of Horror: The Movies That Influenced Generations |date= |year=2022 |isbn=979-8831215076}}</ref>

'''Tayla Jones''' (born 1996) is an Australian off-road motorcycle racer, competing predominantly in endurance racing such as the [[International Six Days Enduro|ISDE]]. Her extensive successful racing career has given her recognition from [[Grand National Cross Country|GNCC racing]] for being representative of women's motorcycling in Australia since 2013, and GNCC considers her to be one of the most successful female off-roaders in recent memory.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Tuesday Toolbox: Tayla Jones |url=https://gnccracing.com/2020/08/18/tuesday-toolbox-tayla-jones?utm_medium=Social&utm_source=Facebook |access-date=2026-06-01 |website=GNCC Racing |language=en}}</ref>

== Overview ==
With an extended family involved in amateur motorsports, Jones was exposed to biking on a [[Yamaha PW50|PW 50]] since age 4. In interviews she regularly expresses thanks for her parents and sponsors who have enabled and supported her motorcycling career, including her wife and fellow competitor Allie Spurgeon-Jones. Debuting her career at age 16, she accomplished wins in Motocross, Super Moto, and Australian National Endurocross before moving to the US in 2017<ref>{{Cite web |title=Tayla Jones Signs With Rocky Mountain ATV*MC/KR4 |url=https://gnccracing.com/2016/12/28/tayla-jones-signs-with-rocky-mountain-atvmckr4?utm_medium=Social&utm_source=Facebook |access-date=2026-06-01 |website=GNCC Racing |language=en}}</ref> to compete in the top US national off-roading championships, specialising in enduro sports.

Jones has a determined and motivated attitude to the sport despite several setbacks. She expresses in interviews after injuries in 2022 and 2025 that it does not marr her passion for the sport. She told GNCC interviewer in 2022 that "pain is temporary, glory is forever",<ref>{{Cite web |title=Tuesday Toolbox: Tayla Jones |url=https://gnccracing.com/2020/01/28/tuesday-toolbox-tayla-jones?utm_medium=Social&utm_source=Facebook |access-date=2026-06-01 |website=GNCC Racing |language=en}}</ref> and explained in a 2020 interview how she maintains her drive. Jones said she doesn't "believe champions are made without rough patches", which adds fuel to her fire.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Tuesday Toolbox: Tayla Jones |url=https://gnccracing.com/2020/08/18/tuesday-toolbox-tayla-jones?utm_medium=Social&utm_source=Facebook |access-date=2026-06-02 |website=GNCC Racing |language=en}}</ref> This mindset keeps her competing and keen to inspire young women to join the sport.

== Achievements ==
Jones loves sprint enduro style racing, and is a 6-time champion.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Fattore |first=Mark |date=2023-08-16 |title=2023 Australian ISDE team announced |url=https://www.ma.org.au/2023-isde-team-australia-announced/ |access-date=2026-06-01 |website=Motorcycling Australia |language=en-US}}</ref> She won six [[Fédération Internationale de Motocyclisme|FIM]] [[FIM Endurance World Championship|ISDE]] competitions in a row in the female categories between 2013 and 2018.<ref name="auto">{{Cite web |title=Australian Motorsports Hall of Fame Inducts Tayla Jones |url=https://gnccracing.com/2025/04/18/australian-motorsports-hall-of-fame-inducts-tayla-jones?utm_medium=Social&utm_source=Facebook |access-date=2026-06-01 |website=GNCC Racing |language=en}}</ref> This streak resulted in her being awarded [[American Motorcyclist Association|AMA]] female racer of the year award in 2017.<ref>{{Cite web |date=2018-01-23 |title=Tayla Jones awarded 2017 AMA Female Racer - Fullnoise.com.au Motorcycle News |url=https://www.fullnoise.com.au/fullnoise-news/tayla-jones-awarded-2017-ama-female-racer/ |access-date=2026-06-01 |language=en-AU}}</ref>

Following her move to the US, she won 3 [[Grand National Cross Country|GNCC]] WXC titles from 2017 to 2019.<ref name="auto"/> After suffering an injury to her hand in 2020 during a Full Gas Sprint Enduro competition she maintained motivation to compete in the rest of the sport season.

In 2022, visa issues prevented Jones from competing in the ISDE as part of the Australian women's team, being replaced by Ebony Nielson after her forced withdrawal.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Pearson |first=Jon |date=2022-07-14 |title=ISDE 2022: Visa issues force Tayla Jones out of Team Australia |url=https://enduro21.com/en/racing/latest/isde/isde-2022-visa-issues-force-tayla-jones-out-of-team-australia |access-date=2026-06-02 |website=Enduro21 |language=en-gb}}</ref>

Jones suffered a second major injury to her leg in 2025 during that season's GNCC round, leading to her withdrawal from that year's ISDE and further GNCC racing. She was replaced by Madison Healey in the 2025 ISDE team, and remains in recovery.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Pearson |first=Jon |date=2025-07-09 |title=Madison Healey replaces injured Jones in Australia's ISDE Women's Team |url=https://enduro21.com/en/racing/latest/isde/madison-healey-replaces-injured-jones-in-australia-s-isde-women-s-team |access-date=2026-06-02 |website=Enduro21 |language=en-gb}}</ref> Jones remains committed to racing and women's inclusion in the sport overall, and was inducted into the Australian Motorsports Hall of Fame in April 2025, which recognises individuals who have made significant contributions to Australian motorsports.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Australian Motorsports Hall of Fame Inducts Tayla Jones |url=https://gnccracing.com/2025/04/18/australian-motorsports-hall-of-fame-inducts-tayla-jones?utm_medium=Social&utm_source=Facebook |access-date=2026-06-02 |website=GNCC Racing |language=en}}</ref>

== Early life, education, career and family ==
Ana Lucía Pineda Aruachan was born on 8 October 1987 in [[Montería]], Córdoba.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.elheraldo.co/politica/2026/06/21/ella-es-ana-lucia-pineda-la-nueva-primera-dama-de-colombia/|title=Ella es Ana Lucía Pineda, la nueva primera dama de Colombia|access-date=June 28, 2026|date=June 21, 2026|work=[[El Heraldo (Colombia)|El Heraldo]]}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.noticiascaracol.com/politica/elecciones-colombia/ella-es-ana-lucia-pineda-la-empresaria-que-sera-la-proxima-primera-dama-de-colombia-cb20|title=Ella es Ana Lucía Pineda, la empresaria que será la próxima primera dama de Colombia|access-date=June 27, 2026|date=June 21, 2026|work=[[EFE]]|publisher=[[Noticias Caracol]]}}</ref> Her father, Gabriel Pineda, served as the livestock technical secretary at Colombian Federation of Cattle Ranchers. Her mother, Regina Aruachan, served as the [[consul general]] in Miami under the [[Presidency of Iván Duque|Duque administration]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://lalenguacaribe.co/2019/nacional/la-monteriana-regina-aruachan-es-la-nueva-consul-de-colombia-en-estados-unidos/|title=La monteriana Regina Aruachan es la nueva cónsul de Colombia en Estados Unidos|access-date=June 27, 2026|date=February 14, 2019|work=La Lengua Caribe}}</ref> Ana Lucía has a [[twin sister]], María Victoria, as well as an older brother, José Gabriel, and an older sister, Lilian.

The family enjoyed a comfortable economic position in Montería. As a child, she attended the British School of Montería, as did her siblings, where she completed high school, excelling in [[mathematics]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.tropicanafm.com/2026/ella-es-ana-lucia-pineda-esposa-de-abelardo-de-la-espriella-se-conocen-desde-ninos-460521.html|title=Ella es Ana Lucía Pineda, esposa de Abelardo De La Espriella: se conocen desde niños|access-date=June 4, 2026|date=June 3, 2026|last=Contreras|first=Margarita|website=Tropicana Colombia}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.las2orillas.co/la-joven-monteriana-esposa-de-abelardo-de-la-espriella-a-quien-la-vida-le-dio-un-vuelco-total/|title=La joven monteriana, esposa de Abelardo de la Espriella, a quien la vida le dio un vuelco total|access-date=June 3, 2026|date=January 30, 2026|work=[[Las2orillas]]}}</ref><ref name=":1" >{{Cite web|url=https://www.semana.com/politica/articulo/quien-es-ana-lucia-pineda-la-esposa-de-abelardo-de-la-espriella-candidato-por-la-presidencia-en-colombia/202645/|title=¿Quién es Ana Lucía Pineda, la esposa de Abelardo de la Espriella, candidato por la presidencia en Colombia?|access-date=June 2, 2026|date=May 31, 2026|work=[[Semana]]}}</ref> After graduating at seventeen, Ana Lucía enrolled in the Faculty of Economic and Administrative Sciences at the [[Pontificia Universidad Javeriana]] in Bogotá, D.C., from which she finally graduated {{Circa}} 2006 and 2007.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://canaltrece.com.co/noticias/asi-son-ana-lucia-pineda-y-pilar-rueda-las-mujeres-que-aspiran-a-la-casa-de-narino/|title=Así son Ana Lucía Pineda y Pilar Rueda, las mujeres que aspiran a la Casa de Nariño|access-date=June 3, 2026|date=June 1, 2026|last=Rubiano|first=Johanna|work=[[Canal Trece]]}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=https://caracol.com.co/2026/06/02/quienes-son-pilar-rueda-y-ana-lucia-pineda-una-de-ellas-sera-la-proxima-primera-dama/|title=¿Quiénes son Pilar Rueda y Ana Lucía Pineda? Una de ellas será la próxima primera dama|access-date=June 3, 2026|date=June 1, 2026|last=León|first=Marylin|work=[[Caracol Radio]]}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=https://panamanoticiasnetwork.com/mundo/la-familia-de-abelardo-de-la-espriella-quien-es-ana-lucia-pineda/|title=La Familia de Abelardo De La Espriella:Quién es Ana Lucía Pineda|access-date=May 30, 2026|date=May 26, 2026|work=Panama Noticias Network}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.minuto60.com/elecciones-2026/ella-es-ana-lucia-pineda-esposa-abelardo-espriela/9931|title=Historia y perfil de Ana Lucía Pineda, esposa de Abelardo de la Espriella: negocios y más|access-date=June 2, 2026|date=May 31, 2026|last=Ruiz|first=Vannesa|work=Minuto 60}}</ref>

Pineda met De La Espriella when she was 5 and Abelardo was 15.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.semana.com/confidenciales/articulo/esposa-de-abelardo-de-la-espriella-sorprendio-con-revelacion-sobre-los-primeros-dias-de-su-romance/202656/|title=Esposa de Abelardo De La Espriella sorprendió con revelación sobre los primeros días de su romance|access-date=July 5, 2026|date=June 20, 2026|work=[[Semana]]}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.infobae.com/colombia/2026/03/27/abelardo-de-la-espriella-explico-como-paso-de-ateo-a-activista-religioso-tuve-un-proceso-hace-seis-anos/|title=Abelardo de la Espriella explicó cómo pasó de ateo a activista religioso: “Tuve un proceso hace seis años”|access-date=June 20, 2026|date=March 27, 2026|last=Correa|first=Juan Manuel|work=[[Infobae]]}}</ref><ref name=":1" /> They met again 14 years later, when she was 18 and De la Espriella 29, in a meeting arranged by their families. Pineda began a relationship with De La Espriella in 2005.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.elpais.com.co/colombia/asi-nacio-la-historia-de-amor-de-abelardo-de-la-espriella-y-su-esposa-ana-lucia-pineda-detalles-de-su-relacion-0812.html|title=Así nació la historia de amor de Abelardo de la Espriella y su esposa, Ana Lucía Pineda: detalles de su relación|access-date=June 29, 2026|date=June 8, 2026|last=Fiallo|first=Johana|work=[[El País (Cali)|El País]]}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.semana.com/politica/articulo/abelardo-de-la-espriella-y-ana-lucia-pineda-revelan-como-empezo-su-amor-su-mama-nos-puso-una-cita-en-la-oficina-y-nos-reencontramos/202609/|title=Abelardo de la Espriella y Ana Lucía Pineda revelan cómo empezó su amor: “Su mamá nos puso una cita en la oficina y nos reencontramos”|access-date=June 30, 2026|date=May 27, 2026|work=[[Semana]]}}</ref> They married on December 13, 2008, at the [[Iglesia de San Pedro Claver, Cartagena|San Pedro Claver Church]] in [[Cartagena, Colombia|Cartagena]].

In 2011, Ana Lucía and Abelardo had a daughter, Lucía de la Espriella. Ana Lucía chose her name in her honor. After Lucía's birth, Ana Lucía had Salvador, followed approximately three years later by Filippo, and in 2023, her youngest daughter, Francesca.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://elcomercio.pe/mundo/latinoamerica/abelardo-de-la-espriella-quien-es-ana-lucia-pineda-la-empresaria-que-sera-la-proxima-primera-dama-de-colombia-perfil-noticia/|title=Quién es Ana Lucía Pineda, la empresaria que será la próxima primera dama de Colombia|access-date=June 28, 2026|date=June 21, 2026|work=[[El Comercio (Peru)|El Comercio]]}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=https://cronicadelquindio.com/actualidad/colombia/quien-es-ana-lucia-pineda-la-proxima-primera-dama-de-colombia/|title=Quién es Ana Lucía Pineda, la próxima primera dama de Colombia|access-date=June 28, 2026|date=June 22, 2026|work=La Crónica del Quindío}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.noticiasrcn.com/colombia/quien-es-la-esposa-de-abelardo-de-la-espriella-la-primera-dama-de-colombia-1032975|title=¿Quién es la esposa de Abelardo de la Espriella, la nueva primera dama de Colombia?|access-date=June 28, 2026|date=June 22, 2026|last=Díaz|first=Yhonay|work=Noticias RCN}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.besame.fm/2026/ella-es-la-hermosa-esposa-de-abelardo-de-la-espriella-tienen-4-hijos-y-se-llevan-10-anos-238543.html|title=Ana Lucía Pineda, la esposa de Abelardo de la Espriella, ¿quién es? == First Lady of Colombia (2026-present) ==
Ana Lucía is the sixth youngest first lady of Colombia after [[Ana Milena Muñoz de Gaviria]].

=== Official duties ===
During the initial days of her term as first lady, Ana Lucía traveled with President de la Espriella to [[Cali]], [[Valle del Cauca]], following the serious damage caused by the [[2026 Colombia earthquake]], from where she led the reconstruction of the affected areas.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.elpais.com.co/colombia/ana-lucia-pineda-liderara-reconstruccion-tras-terremoto-de-74-en-colombia-estas-son-sus-primeras-acciones-1127.html|title=Ana Lucía Pineda liderará reconstrucción tras terremoto de 7,4 en Colombia: estas son sus primeras acciones|access-date=August 11, 2026|date=August 11, 2026|last=Martínez|first=Kevin Mauricio|work=[[El País (Cali)|El País]]}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.semana.com/confidenciales/articulo/terremoto-en-colombia-la-primera-dama-ana-lucia-pineda-anuncia-puntos-de-acopio-de-ayudas-no-estan-solos/202613/|title=Terremoto en Colombia: la primera dama, Ana Lucía Pineda, anuncia puntos de acopio de ayudas. “No están solos”|access-date=August 11, 2026|date=August 11, 2026|work=[[Semana]]}}</ref>

As a student at Columbia College, Avila Chevalier organized with [[Students for Justice in Palestine]] and Mobilized African Diaspora. In 2014 Avila Chevalier lived in the Palestinian city of [[Nablus]] for around two months while interning for [[Tomorrow's Youth Organization]] to teach English to Palestinian toddlers and children. The [[2014 Gaza War]] started shortly after she returned to the US. Her research has focused on [[List of United States immigration and nationality laws|immigration law]] and [[Immigration policy of the United States|policy]] and [[incarceration in the United States]], especially on the ways Black immigrants from [[Latin America]] have been affected by the US criminal justice system and deportation.{{cite web |title= Darializa Avila Chevalier |url= https://www.sadrjohnjay.com/artists/darializa-avila-chevalier-ml9am |access-date= February 7, 2026 |website= Social Anatomy of a Deportation Regime |publisher= John Jay College of Criminal Justice, [[CUNY]]}} == Early career and activism == ===Black Youth Project 100=== {{see|Black Youth Project 100}} After graduating from Columbia, Avila Chevalier organized with [[Black Youth Project 100]]. In 2018, the group demanded removal of a [[Central Park]] statue of [[J. Marion Sims]], a 19th-century gynecologist who forcibly subjected enslaved Black women to experiments involving painful surgical techniques without anesthesia, despite later administering anesthesia to his white patients.{{cite news |last1=Wimbish |first1= Whitney Curry |title= Justice Dems Pick Longtime Organizer to Take Harlem |url= https://prospect.org/2025/11/20/darializa-avila-chevalier-harlem-new-york-city-congress-justice-dems/ |access-date= February 7, 2026 |publisher= [[The American Prospect]] |date= November 20, 2025}} Avila Chevalier and three other Black women protested in front of the statue dressed in blood-stained hospital gowns, reading passages from Sims's autobiography, medical journals, and other historical material that highlighted his dehumanization of enslaved women.{{cite news |last1= Escalante |first1= Alejandro S. |title= Gynecology and the Ungendering of Black Women |url= https://www.aaihs.org/gynecology-and-the-ungendering-of-black-women/ |access-date= February 8, 2026 |publisher= African American Intellectual Historical Society |date=December 4, 2018}} The statue was moved later that year.{{cite news |last1= Domonoske |first1= Camila | title= 'Father Of Gynecology,' Who Experimented On Slaves, No Longer On Pedestal In NYC |access-date= June 3, 2026 |publisher= NPR |date= April 17, 2018 |url= https://www.npr.org/sections/thetwo-way/2018/04/17/603163394/-father-of-gynecology-who-experimented-on-slaves-no-longer-on-pedestal-in-nyc}} ===Families for Freedom=== In 2019, as an organizer for Families for Freedom, Avila Chevalier protested to free Abdikadir Mohamed Felt, a Somali immigrant affected by President [[Donald Trump]]'s "[[Executive Order 13769|Muslim ban]]", from [[United States Immigration and Customs Enforcement]] (ICE) detention.{{cite web |last1= Hussain |first1= Murtaza |title= His Visa Was Stamped, His Papers in Order. Immigration courts and detention centers have, for decades, been an abuse of administrative power. By targeting Mahmoud, Trump is now taking this abuse of power to a whole new level and making an example of him to silence those speaking out for the lives and human rights of Palestinians.
=== Policing and public safety === Avila Chevalier supports [[prison abolition]]. She has said she wants to help transform the United States into a society without murders by investing in programs for mental health services, healthcare, housing, and social systems. She acknowledged incarceration for murderers is "just the reality of what is going to happen", but said she was presenting "a vision for what we should have". Avila Chevalier praised Mamdani's effort to create the Department of Community Safety, and said crime reduction correlates with funding for social safety nets. ====Criticisms of the NYPD==== In October 2026, Chevalier called for the removal of [[Jessica Tisch]] as New York City [[police commissioner]], saying, "The [[New York City Police Department|NYPD]]’s Strategic Response Group must be disbanded as quickly as possible, and Commissioner Tisch must step down." Chevalier's comments came in response to the shooting of a suspected [[Illegal immigration|illegal immigrant]] by an [[United States Immigration and Customs Enforcement|Immigration and Customs Enforcement]] officer, which took place in the city. Protests, which Chevalier participated in, occurred in the wake of the shooting and the NYPD deployed officers to manage the situation. During an incident between protesters and police, video footage showed Chevalier falling to the ground after being pushed by a police officer.{{Cite AV media |url=https://www.youtube.com/shorts/YBhzj2DmWjU |title=Dem nominee on being shoved to ground by NYPD during anti-ice protest |date=2026-10-09 |access-date=2026-10-14 |via=YouTube|type=Video|url-status=live|publisher=CNN}} Chevalier later claimed the NYPD "escalat[ed] violence" between officers and protesters, saying, "[she] was shoved to the ground", and that she "witnessed unmarked law enforcement cars hitting protestors as NYPD officers pushed people out of its path." Chevalier also alleged that Tisch "attempted to justify the shooting" and "spent more time protecting a militia that [had] just shot someone than protecting New Yorkers."{{Cite web |last=Bullis |first=Hailey |date=2026-10-09 |title=New York House candidate calls for head of NYPD to step down after ICE shooting |url=https://www.washingtonexaminer.com/policy/immigration/4760948/darializa-avila-chevalier-jessica-tisch-nypd-new-york-ice-shooting/ |access-date=2026-10-14 |website=Washington Examiner |language=en-US}} === Socialism === Avila Chevalier is a democratic socialist and member of the Democratic Socialists of America. She said she came to her ideology through organizing work, her undergraduate and graduate studies, and the [[Black radical tradition]]. She described democratic socialism as "workers and people in general having ownership and dignity over their lives and their work, and achieving that democratically".{{cite web |title= In Harlem, a Democratic Socialist Takes On the Dem Machine |url= https://jacobin.com/2026/01/avila-chevalier-harlem-bronx-socialism |website= Jacobin |access-date= 29 August 2026}} She denied being a communist, and said the question was a distraction. She posted tweets favorable to communist leaders and Marxism around 2020.{{cite web |title= Deleted tweets on Darializa Avila Chevalier's account had favorable references to communist leaders and Marxism |url= https://www.cnn.com/2026/06/29/politics/darializa-avila-chevalier-communism-tweets |website= CNN |access-date= 29 August 2026}} Also in 2020, she lamented the lack of Marxist literature in public libraries, including by [[Vladimir Lenin]], and reposted a post criticizing "banned books" displays for not including the works of [[Joseph Stalin]]. In 2026, she said that was because she believed in freedom of speech and access to all kinds of thought, especially in the wake of [[Book censorship in the United States|book censorship]]. == Personal life == Avila Chevalier is [[Afro-Latin Americans|Afro-Latina]]. In 2018, she converted to [[Islam]].{{Cite web |last= Edwards |first= Jessy |date= May 29, 2026 |title= Darializa Avila Chevalier Thinks She Can Overthrow the 'Dean of Dominican Elected Officials' |url= https://hellgatenyc.com/darializa-avila-chevalier-congress-espaillat-mamdani-endorsement/ |access-date= June 5, 2026 |website= Hell Gate |language= en}} Since 2023, she has been in a romantic relationship with [[Ramzi Kassem]], who in 2026 became the chief legal counsel in [[Zohran Mamdani]]'s [[Mayoralty of Zohran Mamdani|mayoral administration]].{{Cite web |last= Sterne |first= Peter |date= July 1, 2026 |title= Darializa Avila Chevalier is dating Mamdani's lawyer Ramzi Kassem |url= https://www.cityandstateny.com/personality/2026/07/darializa-avila-chevalier-dating-mamdanis-lawyer-ramzi-kassem/414579/ |access-date= |website= [[City & State]] |language= en|quote= "Ramzi Kassem and I met outside an ICE detention facility, both working to free someone unjustly held," she said in a statement. '''Marc Hanappier''' (born 7 February 1990) is a French [[Excommunication in the Catholic Church|excommunicated]] Catholic [[bishop]] of the [[Society of Saint Pius X|Society of St Pius X]], a [[Traditionalist Catholicism|Traditionalist Catholic]] organization declared to be in [[Schism in Christianity|schism]] from the [[Catholic Church]] by [[Pope Leo XIV]].

He is the youngest of the six SSPX bishops, having been [[Consecration in Christianity#Ordination of bishops|consecrated]] without papal approval, at the age of 36, alongside three others in the [[2026 Écône consecrations]].<ref name="vn" /><ref name="ewtn" /><ref name="CH2" />

== Early life ==    
Hanappier was born in 1990 in France. He comes from a large Catholic family with ten children. Two of his brothers are also [[Priest|priests]] in the SSPX. One of his sisters is a traditionalist [[nun]].<ref name="fpl" />    
    
He studied at traditionalist [[Seminary|seminaries]] in [[Flavigny-sur-Ozerain]] and [[Écône]]. In 2013, he was ordained as a priest for the SSPX.<ref name="fpl" /><ref name="fen" /><ref name="CH" />    
    
== Career ==    
After his ordination, Hanappier worked as a [[teacher]] in France. He taught at Étoile-du-Matin school in [[Bitche]] and Saint-Michel school in [[Châteauroux]]. Later, he spent one year in [[Scotland]] to improve his English and do religious work.<ref name="fpl" /><ref name="fen" />    
    
In 2020, he moved to the [[United States]]. He became a teacher of [[metaphysics]] and [[theology]] at the SSPX seminary in [[Dillwyn, Virginia]].<ref name="fpl" /><ref name="fen" />    
    
=== Bishop ===    
On 26 May 2026, the SSPX announced that Hanappier was chosen to become a bishop.<ref name="fpl" /><ref name="fen" /> [[Pope Leo XIV]] did not agree to this choice. The Pope asked the SSPX not to consecrate him.<ref name="letter" />    
    
On 1 July 2026, Hanappier was [[Consecration in Christianity#Catholic Church|consecrated]] as a bishop during a service in [[Écône]], [[Switzerland]] by [[Alfonso de Galarreta]], with [[Bernard Fellay]] acting as the sole [[co-consecrator]].<ref name="CH" /><ref name="wp" />    
    
Because he was consecrated without a papal mandate, Hanappier was latae sententiae [[excommunication|excommunicated]].<ref name="vn" /><ref name="ewtn" /><ref name="KPK" /> The SSPX does not agree with this excommunication.<ref name="wp" />

'''Sebastián Ciganda Herrero''' (born 30 August 1993) is a Uruguayan [[association football|football]]er who plays as a [[goalkeeper (association football)|goalkeeper]] for [[New Zealand National League]] club [[Auckland City F.C.|Auckland City]].
 
==Early life==
Ciganda began playing football as a [[Forward (association football)|striker]] in his hometown of [[José Enrique Rodó, Uruguay|José Enrique Rodó]] with Talleres, before joining Fraternidad FC. In his second game there, he played as a goalkeeper as the team didn't have one.<ref name="Futbol">{{cite web |last1=de León |first1=Gonzalo |title=De no quedar en Nacional a estar en un Mundial de Clubes: la historia de Sebastián Ciganda |url=https://www.montevideo.com.uy/Deportes/De-no-quedar-en-Nacional-a-estar-en-un-Mundial-de-Clubes-la-historia-de-Sebastian-Ciganda-uc910292 |website=futbol.com.uy |access-date=12 July 2026 |language=es |date=31 December 2024 |trans-title=From not making the cut at Nacional to playing in a Club World Cup: the story of Sebastián Ciganda}}</ref>

==Career==
Shortly before his 18th birthday, he went to Montevideo to train with Uruguayan club [[Club Nacional de Football|Nacional]], but was rejected after a month. Afterwards, an acquaintance managed to get him to join [[Centro Atlético Fénix|Fénix]], but Ciganda stopped going as he couldn't keep up with the training schedule while also studying journalism.<ref name="Futbol"/>

In 2016, at the age of 22, he moved to New Zealand after obtaining a working holiday visa, working in the [[Kiwifruit|kiwi]] harvest in a small town. While there, he got in contact with an Argentinian, who got him connected to football in the country, mostly playing at a local level with other Uruguayans. Shortly after, he moved to [[Waiheke Island]], and began to play for [[Waiheke United AFC|Waiheke United]], spending six seasons at the club.<ref name="Futbol"/>

In 2021, he helped Waiheke United win the [[NRFL Championship]], earning promotion to the [[New Zealand National League]]. He remained with the club in [[2022 New Zealand National League|2022]], after the introductions of a foreign-player limit. His performances that season caught the attention of [[Auckland City F.C.|Auckland City]], who signed him in July 2023,<ref>{{cite web |title=Goalkeeper's move to Auckland City increases pressure on struggling Waiheke |url=https://www.friendsoffootballnz.com/2023/07/07/goalkeepers-move-to-auckland-city-increases-pressure-on-struggling-waiheke/ |website=Friends of Football |access-date=12 July 2026 |language=en-NZ |date=7 July 2023}}</ref> although remained on Waiheke Island due to his job.<ref name="Futbol"/>

At Auckland City, Ciganda was the club's third-choice goalkeeper, making only one appearance for the club in a [[exhibition match|friendly]] prior to the [[2023 FIFA Club World Cup]].<ref name="Futbol"/> He was included in their squad for the tournament,<ref name="CWC">{{cite web |title=FIFA Club World Cup Saudi Arabia 2023™: Squad List |url=https://fdp.fifa.org/assetspublic/ce119/pdf/SquadLists-English.pdf |website=[[FIFA]] |access-date=12 July 2026 |date=19 December 2023}}</ref> but didn't make an appearance as they lost 3–0 in their only match to [[Al-Ittihad Club (Jeddah)|Al-Ittihad]].<ref name="Futbol"/>

In 2024, he returned to Waiheke United.<ref name="Futbol"/> In June 2025, he returned to Auckland City,<ref>{{cite web |title=El uruguayo que fichó por Auckland City y disputará su segundo Mundial de Clubes |url=https://www.montevideo.com.uy/Deportes/El-uruguayo-que-ficho-por-Auckland-City-y-disputara-su-segundo-Mundial-de-Clubes-uc926805 |website=futbol.com.uy |access-date=12 July 2026 |language=es |date=12 June 2025 |trans-title=The Uruguayan who signed for Auckland City and will play in his second Club World Cup}}</ref> and was included in their squad for the [[2025 FIFA Club World Cup]].<ref>{{cite web |title=FIFA Club World Cup 2025™: Squad List |url=https://fdp.fifa.org/assetspublic/ce233/pdf/SquadLists-English.pdf |website=[[FIFA]] |access-date=12 July 2026 |pages=5 |date=4 July 2025}}</ref>

'''Honami Yano''' (矢野ほなみ, ''Yano Honami'', born 1991) is a Japanese animation director.<ref name="quinzaine">{{cite web |url=https://www.quinzaine-cineastes.fr/en/director/honami-yano |title=Honami Yano |website=Directors' Fortnight |access-date=2026-07-11}}</ref><ref name="imaginaria" /> Her honors include the Ottawa International Animation Festival's Grand Prize for Short Animation and a New Face Award from the Japan Media Arts Festival, both for her 2021 short ''A Bite of Bone''. Yano created the ending animation for the television series ''[[Trigun Stampede]]'' in 2023, and her short film ''Eri'' was selected for the Directors' Fortnight at the Cannes Film Festival in 2026.

== Biography ==
After undergraduate studies in Kyoto that included an exchange at the Rhode Island School of Design, Yano trained under [[Kōji Yamamura]] at Tokyo University of the Arts' Graduate School of Film and New Media.<ref name="imaginaria">{{cite web |url=https://imaginaria.eu/en/a-bite-of-bone/ |title=A Bite of Bone |website=Imaginaria |access-date=2026-07-11}}</ref> Her thesis film, ''Chromosome Sweetheart'' (2017), received nominations at Frameline and other festivals.<ref name="imaginaria" /> In 2021, she joined Nagoya University as a Designated Assistant Professor within the Institutes of Innovation for Future Society.<ref name="imaginaria" /> Her work frequently addresses questions of gender and sexuality, and she has curated screenings devoted to queer animation.<ref name="quinzaine" />

Yano's early short film was ''A Wild Pants Chase'' (パンツをめぐる冒険, 2014).<ref name="newnew">{{cite web |url=https://new-new.jp/en/artist/yano-honami/ |title=Yano Honami |publisher=new-new.jp |access-date=2026-07-12}}</ref>

Running 9 minutes and 45 seconds, her 2021 short film ''A Bite of Bone'' (骨噛み, ''Honekami'') shows a girl at her father's funeral looking back on the final summer the two spent together. The film was produced by Kōji Yamamura and Sunae as the inaugural production of the studio Au Praxinoscope.<ref name="imaginaria" /> ''A Bite of Bone'' won the Grand Prize for Short Animation at the 45th Ottawa International Animation Festival (OIAF) in 2021,<ref name="ann-bone">{{cite web |url=https://www.animenewsnetwork.com/news/2021-10-05/honami-yano-a-bite-of-bone-animated-short-wins-award-at-ottawa-intl-animation-festival/.178110 |title=Honami Yano's "A Bite of Bone" Animated Short Wins Award at Ottawa Int'l Animation Festival |website=Anime News Network |date=October 5, 2021 |access-date=2026-07-12}}</ref><ref name="animag">{{cite web |url=https://www.animationmagazine.net/2021/11/point-by-point-honami-yano-discusses-her-ottawa-grand-prize-film-a-bite-of-bone/ |title=Point by Point: Honami Yano Discusses Her Ottawa Grand Prize Film 'A Bite of Bone' |website=Animation Magazine |date=November 13, 2021 |access-date=2026-07-12}}</ref> the New Face Award in the Animation Division of the 25th Japan Media Arts Festival, the Best Short Animation award at the 29th Raindance Film Festival, and the Gold Award (Animation category) at the 27th ifva Awards, among other festival honors.<ref name="praxinoscope">{{cite web |url=http://praxinoscope.jp/Jp_Studio_Honekami.html |title=骨嚙み |publisher=Au Praxinoscope |access-date=2026-07-12 |language=ja}}</ref> The festival jury commended the film for combining "traditional techniques" with a dot-based visual style that allows the audience to "freely cross places and memories."<ref name="ann-bone" />

In 2023, Yano created the ending animation for the television anime ''[[Trigun Stampede]]''.<ref name="newnew" />

In 2026, her new short film ''Eri'' (also known as ''Eri, the Cow'') was selected for the Directors' Fortnight (Quinzaine des Cinéastes) at the Cannes Film Festival.<ref name="deadline">{{cite web |url=https://deadline.com/2026/04/cannes-directors-fortnight-unveils-2026-lineup-1236860043/ |title=Cannes Directors’ Fortnight Unveils Starry 2026 Lineup |website=Deadline |first=Melanie |last=Goodfellow |date=April 14, 2026 |access-date=2026-07-11}}</ref><ref name="quinzaine" /> The film is set in a world where cows that do not bear calves cannot remain, and follows a Holstein cow who falls in love with another female.<ref name="cartooncontender">{{cite web |url=https://cartooncontender.com/news-and-reviews/animated-features-and-shorts-announced-2026-cannes-directors-fortnight |title=Animated Features & Shorts Announced for 2026 Cannes Directors' Fortnight |website=Cartoon Contender |access-date=2026-07-11}}</ref>

'''Yuki Takeda''' is a Japanese [[whistling|whistler]], musician, and [[Youtuber]] from [[Tokyo, Japan]]. He won two categories in 2010 and one in 2011 performing at the [[International Whistlers Convention]] in [[Louisburg, North Carolina]] as a teenager before winning in 2014 as an adult.<ref name=":0">{{cite web |title=Yuki Takeda |url=https://www.ragnet.co.jp/media/music/author/takeda-yuki#google_vignette |website=RAG Music |access-date=July 19, 2026}}</ref>

== Early life ==
Takeda was born in [[Tokyo, Japan]] in 1992.<ref name=":1">{{cite web |title=想像以上に口笛の世界は広い！『口笛のはなし』発売のお知らせ |url=https://www.mishimaga.com/books/tokushu/006580.html |website=Mishimaga |access-date=July 19, 2026}}</ref> His family moved to [[Toronto, Ontario]] in [[Canada]] when he was 7 due to his mom getting a teaching job at the [[University of Toronto]].<ref name=":2">{{cite web |title=ー映画『Whistle』口笛奏者・武田裕煕さん｜トロント国際映画祭｜特集インタビュー 2025年11月8日 【第50回トロント国際映画祭インタビュー】口笛の世界大会の模様を追った ドキュメンタリー映画『Whistle』口笛奏者・武田裕煕さん｜トロント国際映画祭｜特集インタビュー |url=https://torja.ca/whistle-yuki-takeda |website=TORJA Magazine |access-date=July 19, 2026}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |title=Mario Kart 64: Frappe Snowland ft. a Special Guest! |url=https://www.patreon.com/extralivesmusic/posts/mario-kart-64-ft-45307813 |website=Patreon |access-date=July 19, 2026}}</ref> He learned how to whistle at age 10, after seeing friends do it and teaching himself by watching videos.<ref name=":3">{{cite web |last1=Lindholm |first1=Jane |title=Summer School: How To Whistle |url=https://www.vermontpublic.org/vpr-news/2014-06-09/summer-school-how-to-whistle |website=Vermont Public |access-date=July 19, 2026}}</ref> During middle school, he traveled to [[The Netherlands]] for work, where he started whistling more serious due to boredom while at home.<ref name=":2" /> He returned to Japan for school and graduated from [[Tokyo Gakugei University Senior High School]].<ref name=":4">{{cite web |title=世界中に友達ができる |url=https://grew-bancroft.or.jp/message/1208/ |website=Grew Bancroft |access-date=July 19, 2026}}</ref>

He originally went to the [[University of Tokyo]] before transferring to [[Middlebury College]] in [[Middlebury, Vermont]], where he got his BA in African Studies and lived in [[Cameroon]] for a little bit during his studies.<ref name=":2" /><ref>{{cite web |title=Potential of whistling as instrumental music |url=https://tedxutokyo.com/en/speaker/yuki-takeda |website=TED Talk Tokyo |access-date=July 19, 2026}}</ref> While at Middlebury, a senior project he did focused on whistling, performing at concerts and teaching different types of whistles for the Vermont Edition Summer School, including glissando, trills, and double tones—singing two notes at once.<ref name=":3" /><ref>{{cite web |last1=de Seife |first1=Ethan |title=A Middlebury College Student Takes Whistling to a New Level |url=https://www.sevendaysvt.com/arts-culture/a-middlebury-college-student-takes-whistling-to-a-new-level-2355599/ |website=Seven Days |access-date=July 19, 2026}}</ref>

== Career ==
When Takeda was 16, he saw the winners of a whistling competition being scored and interviewed on [[TBS Television (Japan)|TBS]]'s "Let's Go To School!" program,<ref name=":2" /> with one contestant catching his eye. The boy, who was named Takumi Gima,<ref name=":5">{{cite web |last1=Suzuki |first1=Yo |title=2025年5月31日第144回ゲスト 口笛奏者/ウィスリング研究家・武田裕煕さん |url=https://www.tfm.co.jp/koh/report/119125 |website=Kiss Our Humanity |access-date=July 19, 2026}}</ref> talked about being able to whistle three-octaves, which Takeda attempted and succeeded.<ref>{{cite web |last1=Bateman |first1=Oliver Lee |title=Elite Competitive Whistlers Put Their Lips to the Ultimate Test |url=https://melmagazine.com/en-us/story/elite-competitive-whistlers-put-their-lips-to-the-ultimate-test |website=MEL Magazine |access-date=July 19, 2026}}</ref> While at Middlebury, he performed with his band, 'Yuki Takeda & Friends', where he whistled and also played the [[alto saxophone]].<ref>{{cite web |title=Yuki Takeda & Friends |url=https://www.middlebury.edu/events/event/yuki-takeda-friends-0 |website=Middlebury |access-date=July 19, 2026}}</ref>

Growing up, Takeda learned different instruments including the [[acoustic guitar]], [[piano]], and [[cuatro]]{{Disambiguation needed|date=August 2026}}.<ref name=":5" /><ref name=":2" /> He was inspired by [[Yosuke Yamashita]] to get into [[jazz music]] and also is into Venezuelan Folk music.<ref>{{cite web |title=Suginami Public Relations, October 15, 2022 Issue, Pages 1-3 |url=https://www.city.suginami.tokyo.jp/documents/2987/suginami-1015-1-3.pdf |website=Suginami |access-date=July 19, 2026}}</ref> Other instruments he learned includes [[cajon]], [[flute]], and [[maracas]].<ref name=":6">{{cite web |title=Judges Profiles |url=https://whistlersguild.org/competitions/gwc-iv/gwc-iv-judge-profiles/ |website=Whistlers Guild |access-date=July 19, 2026}}</ref>

In 2010, Takeda won the "Teen Division" in the International Whistlers Convention, where fellow whistler and the vocalist for the band [[Novelbright]] [[Yūdai Takenaka]] won with him.<ref name=":5" />

Since 2022, Takeda was the organizer for the [[Global Whistling Championship]].<ref>{{cite web |title=口笛世界大会が4年ぶりに日本で開催　スペシャル・コンサートやシンポジウム開催も |url=https://www.cdjournal.com/news/-/99636 |website=Culture & Discovery Journal |access-date=July 19, 2026}}</ref>

In 2025, Takeda co-wrote a book 'Kuchibue no Hanashi', also known as 'The Story of Whistling', with non-fiction writer Hazuki Saiso (who ironically cannot whistle)<ref>{{cite web |title=『口笛のはなし』　最相葉月、武田裕煕著　ミシマ社　2200円 |url=https://weekly-economist.mainichi.jp/articles/20250408/se1/00m/020/069000d |website=Weekly Economist Online |access-date=July 19, 2026}}</ref> about the history of whistling.<ref>{{cite web |last1=Shimbun |first1=Mainichi |title=武田裕煕さん『口笛のはなし』　世界一が語る魅力満載　最相葉月さんと網羅的に対話 |url=https://mainichi.jp/articles/20250317/dde/014/040/013000c |website=Mainichi |access-date=July 19, 2026}}</ref> Also in 2025, Takeda was one of the whistlers in the documentary "Whistle", which follows those who competes at the [[World Whistling Championship]]. Director [[Christopher Nelius]] made the film which was shown at the 50th annual [[Toronto International Film Festival]].<ref name=":2" />

On his Youtube Channel, Takeda posts whistling covers, tips on how to do different types of whistles, and collabs with different artists, including other whistlers like [https://ja.wikipedia.org/wiki/%E5%8F%A3%E7%AC%9B%E5%A4%AA%E9%83%8E Taro Kuchibue] and other musicians like Jorge Glem, [[Cheo Hurtado]], and David Peña.<ref name=":6" />

Takeda also performs in the group 'Two Cats Two Dogs'.<ref name=":0" />

== Personal life ==
He has a wife who is originally from [[Singapore]] who both lived in [[Philippines|the Philippines]] before the [[COVID-19 pandemic]].<ref name=":2" /> By the time he was 20, Takeda could speak 5 different languages: English, French, Japanese, Portuguese, and Spanish.<ref name=":1" />

Along with whistling, he also works at an animal healthcare company.<ref name=":4" />

'''Erwan Colas''' (born 22 April 1997) is a French [[Association football|footballer]] who plays as a [[Winger (association football)|winger]] for [[Ligue 1]] club [[Le Mans FC|Le Mans]].

== Club career ==
A youth product of the French club [[Chartres Horizon]], in 2018 Colas moved to the American college team [[Stetson Hatters]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.lechorepublicain.fr/chartres-28000/football/erwan-colas-ex-joueur-de-chartres-horizon-raconte-sa-premiere-saison-reussie-aux-etats-unis_13088396/|title=Erwan Colas, ex-joueur de Chartres Horizon, raconte sa première saison réussie aux Etats-Unis|date=19 December 2018|website=L'Écho républicain
}}</ref> He returned to France with [[C'Chartres Football|C'Chartres]] in the [[Championnat National 3]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.latribunemancelle.fr/article/erwan-colas-un-pari-sur-l-avenir|title=Erwan Colas, un pari sur l'avenir|date=27 June 2023|website=La Tribune Mancelle}}</ref> On 6 July 2022, he joined [[FC Lorient|Lorient's reserves]] in the [[Championnat National 2]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.lechorepublicain.fr/chartres-28000/football/l-attaquant-du-c-chartres-football-erwan-colas-signe-chez-les-pros-au-fc-lorient_14155292/|title=L'attaquant du C'Chartres Football Erwan Colas signe chez les pros, au FC Lorient|date=5 July 2022|website=L'Écho républicain}}</ref> He made one single appearance with the senior Lorient team as a substitute in a 6–0 [[Coupe de France]] win over [[AS La Châtaigneraie|La Châtaigneraie]] on 8 January 2023.<ref name="a820">{{cite web | title= | website=espn.in | url=https://www.espn.in/football/match?gameId=657847 | access-date=2026-07-21}}</ref> On 27 July 2023, he transferred to [[Le Mans FC|Le Mans]] in the [[Championnat National]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.lechorepublicain.fr/chartres-28000/sports/le-mainvillois-erwan-colas-s-engage-au-mans-fc-c-est-important-d-aller-dans-un-endroit-ou-on-se-sent-desire_14333805/|title=Football/N1 - Le Mainvillois Erwan Colas s'engage au Mans FC : "C'est important d'aller dans un endroit où on se sent désiré"|first=Centre|last=France|date=27 June 2023}}</ref> After 2 consecutive promotions with Le Mans to [[Ligue 1]], he extended his contract with the club for 3 seasons on 22 June 2026.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://sports.yahoo.com/articles/official-erwan-colas-extends-le-141500815.html|title=Official I Erwan Colas extends Le Mans contract|first=Get French Football News·1 min|last=read|date=22 June 2026|website=Yahoo Sports}}</ref>

==Personal life==
Colas is the son of the football manager and former player [[:fr:Patrice Colas|Patrice Colas]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.lechorepublicain.fr/chartres-28000/football/les-colas-pere-et-fils-en-match-amical-avec-le-fc-drouais-cfa2-et-chartres-horizon-dh_11542528/|title=Les Colas père et fils en match amical avec le FC drouais (CFA2) et Chartres Horizon (DH)|date=6 August 2015|website=L'Écho républicain
}}</ref>

'''Elizabeth Greenwood''' (born October 19, 1999) is an American professional [[baseball]] [[catcher]] and [[Coach (baseball)|coach]]. She currently plays and coaches for the [[Boston Hunters]] of the [[Women's Pro Baseball League]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=Introducing the Managers & Coaching Staff of the Founding Four WPBL Teams |url=https://www.womensprobaseballleague.com/2026/07/29/introducing-the-managers-coaching-staff-of-the-founding-four-wpbl-teams/ |access-date=2026-07-30 |website=Women's Pro Baseball League |language=en-US}}</ref>

== Early life and education ==
Greenwood was raised in [[Amherst, New Hampshire|Amherst]], New Hampshire. She attended [[Souhegan High School]], where she was a catcher on the baseball team.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Ingemi |first=Marisa |date=December 1, 2017 |title=Beth Greenwood stars at Souhegan High |url=https://www.baseballjournal.com/beth-greenwood-stars-at-souhegan-high-n-h/ |access-date=July 28, 2026 |website=New England Baseball Journal |language=en-US}}</ref>

Greenwood attended the [[University of Rochester]], where she played for the baseball team and studied [[electrical engineering]].<ref name=":1">{{Cite web |last=Mandelaro |first=Jim |date=November 30, 2021 |title=Beth Greenwood ’22 in a league of her own |url=https://www.rochester.edu/newscenter/beth-greenwood-league-of-their-own-504262/ |access-date=July 28, 2026 |website=University of Rochester News Center |language=en-US}}</ref> As a [[Rochester Yellowjackets|Yellowjacket]], she was the first female baseball player in university history and the first American female to catch in an [[National Collegiate Athletic Association|NCAA]] baseball game.<ref>{{Cite web |year=2022 |title=Beth Greenwood - Baseball |url=https://uofrathletics.com/sports/baseball/roster/beth-greenwood/7932 |access-date=July 28, 2026 |website=University of Rochester Athletics |language=en}}</ref><ref>{{Cite news |last=Grossfeld |first=Stan |date=July 4, 2022 |title=Baseball pioneer Beth Greenwood continues blazing a trail from behind the plate |url=https://www.bostonglobe.com/2022/07/04/sports/baseball-pioneer-beth-greenwood-continues-blazing-trail-behind-plate/ |access-date=July 28, 2026 |work=[[The Boston Globe]] |language=en-US |issn=0743-1791}}</ref> She graduated in 2022.<ref name=":1" />

== Player career ==
Greenwood joined the [[United States women's national baseball team]] development roster in 2018.<ref name=":0">{{Cite web |title=Beth Greenwood |url=https://www.vassarathletics.com/sports/baseball/roster/coaches/beth-greenwood/1845 |access-date=July 28, 2026 |website=Vassar College Athletics |language=en}}</ref> She made the official roster in 2023.<ref name=":2">{{Cite web |last=Ingemi |first=Marisa |date=July 12, 2026 |title=Beth Greenwood's unexpected path to the WPBL |url=https://www.theixsports.com/features/beth-greenwood-next-chapter-baseball-unexpected-turn-wpbl/ |access-date=July 28, 2026 |website=The IX Sports |language=en-US}}</ref>

Greenwood was selected by [[Boston Hunters|WPBL Boston]] in the third round of the inaugural [[Women's Pro Baseball League|Women’s Pro Baseball League]] draft.<ref>{{Cite web |last=King |first=Tom |date=November 24, 2025 |title=DRAFTED! Amherst’s Greenwood chosen by Boston WPBL team |url=https://www.nashuatelegraph.com/sports/local-sports/2025/11/24/drafted-amhersts-greenwood-chosen-by-boston-wpbl-team/ |access-date=July 28, 2026 |website=[[Nashua Telegraph]] |language=en-US}}</ref>

== Coaching career ==
After graduating in 2022, Greenwood spent two years as a Baseball Research and Development Fellow and development coach for the [[Jersey Shore BlueClaws]], the [[High-A]] affiliate of the [[Philadelphia Phillies]].<ref name=":2" /><ref>{{Cite web |last=Bassett |first=Joyce |date=July 16, 2026 |title=Bassett: Rochester catcher Beth Greenwood makes history in return of women's pro baseball |url=https://www.timesunion.com/sports/article/womens-pro-baseball-league-beth-greenwood-22329941.php |access-date=July 28, 2026 |website=[[Times Union (Albany, New York)|Times Union]] |language=en}}</ref> During the 2025-26 school year, Greenwood was a pitching coach with the baseball program at [[Vassar College]].<ref name=":0" />

On July 29, 2026, it was announced that Greenwood would serve on the [[Boston Hunters]] coaching staff.<ref>{{Cite web |date=July 29, 2026 |title=Introducing the Managers & Coaching Staff of the Founding Four WPBL Teams |url=https://www.womensprobaseballleague.com/2026/07/29/introducing-the-managers-coaching-staff-of-the-founding-four-wpbl-teams/ |access-date=July 29, 2026 |website=[[Women's Pro Baseball League]] |language=en-US}}</ref>

== Activism ==
Greenwood is on the board of Baseball for All (BFA), a non-profit which provides women and girls opportunities to play baseball.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Kreuz |first=Julia |last2=Laible |first2=Anna |date=July 31, 2024 |title=With USWNT & in Minors, Greenwood models perseverance, authenticity |url=https://www.mlb.com/news/team-usa-beth-greenwood-developing-phillies-milbers |access-date=July 28, 2026 |website=[[MLB]] |language=en}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last= |date=February 14, 2020 |title=The Baseball For All Board and Advisors |url=https://baseballforall.com/our-board-and-leadership-team/ |access-date=July 28, 2026 |website=Baseball For All |language=en-US}}</ref> In 2026, Greenwood worked with BFA to host the largest girls' youth baseball tournament in the United States.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Ganley |first=Rick |date=July 28, 2026 |title=She dreamed of playing for the Red Sox. Now, this NH native has a league of her own. |url=https://www.nhpr.org/sports/2026-07-28/boston-hunters-redsox-womens-baseball-league-wpbl |access-date=July 28, 2026 |website=[[New Hampshire Public Radio]] |language=en}}</ref>

== Personal life ==
Greenwood is [[LGBTQ people|LGBTQ+]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=Allen |first=Samantha |date=July 16, 2026 |title=All the LGBTQ+ Players in the Women’s Pro Baseball League — And Where to Follow Them |url=https://www.them.us/culture/wpbl-league-out-lgbtq-players |access-date=July 28, 2026 |website=[[them (magazine)|them]] |language=en}}</ref>

'''Teague Egan''' (born July 6, 1988)<ref name="sportsagentblog">{{cite web |last=Heitner |first=Darren |title=Interview With The Agent: Teague Egan |url=https://sportsagentblog.com/2010/11/27/interview-with-the-agent-teague-egan/ |work=Sports Agent Blog |date=2010-11-27}}</ref> is an American businessman and the founder and chief executive officer of [[Energy Exploration Technologies]] (EnergyX), a lithium extraction technology company.<ref name="wsj">{{cite news |last=Steinberg |first=Julie |title=He Wants to Be the Lithium King. Run for President. And Live to 150. |url=https://www.wsj.com/business/teague-egan-energyx-lithium-1c041366 |newspaper=[[The Wall Street Journal]] |date=2024-10-06 }}</ref><ref name="nytimes">{{cite news |last=Krauss |first=Clifford |title=Green Energy Race Draws an American Underdog to Bolivian Lithium |url=https://www.nytimes.com/2021/12/16/business/energy-environment/bolivia-lithium-electric-cars.html |newspaper=[[The New York Times]] |date=2021-12-16 }}</ref> Egan began his career in music and sports management. In October 2010, aged 22, he became a contract advisor certified by the [[National Football League Players Association]], the first person certified by the union before graduating college; the union revoked his certification that December after he gave an impermissible benefit to a [[USC Trojans football|University of Southern California football]] player.<ref name="usctrojans">{{cite web |last=Moore |first=Jordan |title=Teague Egan Decertified by NFLPA |url=https://usctrojans.com/sports/2017/6/15/blog-2010-12-teague-egan-decertified-by-nflpa-html.aspx |publisher=[[USC Trojans|USC Athletics]] |date=2010-12-03 }}</ref><ref name="nfl">{{cite news |agency=Associated Press |title=NFLPA gives agent nine-month ban for contacting college player |url=https://www.nfl.com/news/nflpa-gives-agent-nine-month-ban-for-contacting-college-player-09000d5d81c9da13 |work=[[National Football League]] |date=2010-12-03 }}</ref> He founded EnergyX in 2018 and has led its development of direct lithium extraction projects in Chile, Texas, Arkansas and Utah.<ref>{{cite news |last=De Chant |first=Tim |title=Exclusive: Why EnergyX raised $75M from small investors, even after taking VC money from GM and others |url=https://techcrunch.com/2024/10/04/why-energyx-raised-75m-from-small-investors-even-after-taking-vc-money-from-gm-and-others/ |work=[[TechCrunch]] |date=2024-10-04 }}</ref><ref>{{cite news |title=EnergyX, Compass Minerals sign MOU for $400M for U.S. lithium plant |url=https://www.axios.com/pro/climate-deals/2026/05/18/energyx-compass-minerals-project-powder-dle-lithium |work=[[Axios (website)|Axios]] |date=2026-05-18 }}</ref>

== Early life and education ==
Egan was born on July 6, 1988 and raised in South Florida. His father, Michael Egan, founded [[Alamo Rent a Car]].<ref name="wsj" /> He attended [[Pine Crest School]] before transferring to [[St. Thomas Aquinas High School (Fort Lauderdale)|St. Thomas Aquinas High School]] in his junior year, where he competed in golf and track.<ref name="sportsagentblog" /> Egan received a bachelor's degree from the [[University of Southern California]] and completed an executive program in exponential technology at [[Singularity University]].<ref>{{cite news |title=Meet the Lithium King Teague Egan |url=https://shalemag.com/meet-the-lithium-king-teague-egan/ |work=Shale Magazine |date=2022-11-04 }}</ref>

==Career==
Egan founded 1st Round Enterprises in 2008 while an undergraduate at USC, promoting music events in Los Angeles. In 2009 he co-founded the independent record label 1st Round Records with Zack Johnson.<ref name="inc">{{cite news |last=Heitner |first=Darren |title=How This Former NFL Agent Survived Failure and Found Startup Success |url=https://www.inc.com/darren-heitner/former-nfl-agent-has-gone-from-failure-to-startup-success.html |work=[[Inc. (magazine)]] |year=2016 }}</ref> The label released ''[[Boston's Boy]]'', the 2010 debut EP by rapper [[Sammy Adams]], which reached number one on the [[iTunes Store|iTunes]] hip-hop chart and number 73 on the ''[[Billboard 200]]''.<ref>{{cite news |title=Rapper Sam Adams Brews Fame on iTunes, Billboard Charts |url=https://www.billboard.com/music/music-news/rapper-sam-adams-brews-fame-on-itunes-billboard-charts-958917/ |work=[[Billboard (magazine)]] |year=2010 }}</ref>

In October 2010, at the age of 22, Egan became a certified contract advisor with the [[National Football League Players Association]] while still an undergraduate, the first person certified by the union before graduating college.<ref name="usctrojans" /> In November 2010, he gave USC running back [[Dillon Baxter]] a ride across campus on a golf cart bearing his company's logo. Baxter was held out of USC's November 20 game against [[Oregon State Beavers football|Oregon State]] and served a one-game suspension for accepting an impermissible benefit; USC head coach [[Lane Kiffin]] described the contact as inadvertent.<ref>{{cite news |agency=Associated Press |title=USC's Baxter Won't Play After Alleged Contact With Agent |url=https://www.cbsnews.com/losangeles/news/uscs-baxter-wont-play-after-alleged-contact-with-agent |work=[[CBS News 24/7]] |date=2010-11-19 }}</ref>

On December 3, 2010, the [[NFL Players Association|NFLPA]] revoked Egan's certification. Union spokesman George Atallah said a review of Egan's qualifications had found he was "not fit to be a certified contract advisor."<ref name="nfl" /> USC vice president of compliance Dave Roberts said the university had been notified promptly and would continue to treat any benefit from Egan to a student-athlete as impermissible under NCAA rules.<ref name="usctrojans" /> Egan subsequently left sports representation.<ref name="inc" />

Egan founded [[Energy Exploration Technologies]] (EnergyX) in 2018 after a visit to the [[Salar de Uyuni]] salt flats in Bolivia, and serves as its chief executive officer and chairman.<ref name="nytimes" /> The company develops [[Lithium#Direct_lithium_extraction|direct lithium extraction]] (DLE) technology and is headquartered in [[San Juan, Puerto Rico]], with laboratory facilities in [[Austin, Texas]]. As of 2024 Egan held approximately 47 percent of the company.<ref name="wsj" /><ref>{{cite news |last=Stringer |first=David |title=Breakthrough Technique Could Produce Lithium in Hours Not Months |url=https://www.bloomberg.com/news/articles/2020-03-09/breakthrough-technique-could-produce-lithium-in-hours-not-months |work=[[Bloomberg News]] |date=2020-03-09}}</ref>

In 2021 EnergyX raised $20 million from Obsidian Acquisition Partners, Helios Capital and other investors, and was one of eight companies shortlisted by the government of Bolivian president [[Luis Arce]] to deploy DLE technology in the country.<ref>{{cite news |last=Hawkins |first=Lori |title=Austin-based EnergyX brings in $20 million for tech development |url=https://www.statesman.com/story/business/2021/05/04/energyx-austin-tech-company-brings-20-million-lithium-battery-development/4924726001/ |newspaper=[[Austin American-Statesman]] |date=2021-05-04 }}</ref> EnergyX deployed a pilot plant at the Salar de Uyuni in December 2021.<ref>{{cite news |title=EnergyX deploys lithium pilot plant in Bolivia |url=https://www.miningmagazine.com/design-build/news/1423650/energyx-deploys-lithium-pilot-plant-in-bolivia |work=[[The Mining Journal (trade magazine)]] |date=2021-12-17 }}</ref> In June 2022, [[Reuters]] reported that EnergyX had been dropped from Bolivia's lithium selection process.<ref>{{cite news |title=American startup EnergyX out of Bolivian lithium race |url=https://www.reuters.com/markets/commodities/american-startup-energyx-out-bolivian-lithium-race-2022-06-09/ |work=[[Reuters]] |date=2022-06-09 }}</ref>

Egan sits on the board of directors of the Thomas E. Smith Foundation and co-founded Dance For Paralysis, its outreach division.<ref>{{cite news |title=Teague Egan, el rey Midas de las energías verdes, cautivado por el litio de Uyuni |url=https://www.paginasiete.bo/economia/2021/12/26/teague-egan-el-rey-midas-de-las-energias-verdes-cautivado-por-el-litio-de-uyuni-319069.html |work=[[Página Siete]] |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20211226094441/https://www.paginasiete.bo/economia/2021/12/26/teague-egan-el-rey-midas-de-las-energias-verdes-cautivado-por-el-litio-de-uyuni-319069.html |archive-date=26 December 2021}}</ref> In 2015 he and Thomas E. Smith completed a 2,109-mile bicycle ride from [[Boston]] to [[Miami]] over 38 days, raising $100,000 for [[The Miami Project to Cure Paralysis]].<ref>{{cite news |last1=Grossfeld |first1=Stan |title=Twice-paralyzed hockey player is on road to find a cure |url=https://www.bostonglobe.com/sports/2015/05/25/twice-paralyzed-hockey-player-road-find-cure/6GSfrDoPnG32polfhMhqTM/story.html |work=[[The Boston Globe]] |date=26 May 2015}}</ref>

Furthermore, he starred in many commercial campaigns, with the most famous being the "Amazon Yeti" for [[Amazon (company)|Amazon's]] [[Black Friday (shopping)|Black Friday]] campaign.{{Cite web |last=Hadeeqa |title=Trevor Newlin |url=https://www.nyfa.edu/alumni/trevor-newlin/ |access-date=2026-08-27 |website=NYFA |language=en-US}}{{Cite web |title=How a theater kid from East Texas became a monster |url=https://texasstandard.org/stories/trevor-newlin-actor-alien-romulus-xenomorph-east-texas-kilgore/ |access-date=2026-08-27 |website=Texas Standard |language=en-US}} == Biography == Newlin was born on October 14, 1996, in [[Longview, Texas|Longview]], [[Texas]]. He moved to [[Los Angeles]] to pursue a career in acting, and he graduated from the [[New York Film Academy]] in 2019.{{Cite web |last=Staff |title=Trevor Newlin |url=https://www.nyfa.edu/alumni/trevor-newlin/ |access-date=2026-08-27 |website=NYFA |language=en-US}} He is 6'7" tall.{{Cite web |title=Trevor Newlin |url=https://tvtropes.org/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/Creator/TrevorNewlin |access-date=2026-08-27 |website=TV Tropes}} He was mentored by actor [[Doug Jones (actor)|Doug Jones]] (better known as the Faun in ''[[Pan's Labyrinth]]'', the Amphibian Man in ''[[The Shape of Water]]'' and Saru from ''[[Star Trek: Discovery]]'') who helped him improve his craft as a monster actor and performer. == References == == External links == * [https://www.imdb.com/name/nm9026428/ Newlin] at [[IMDb]] * [https://www.instagram.com/trevor_newlin/ Newlin] at [[Instagram]] {{authority control}} {{DEFAULTSORT:Newlin, Trevor}} [[Category:Living people]] [[Category:1996 births]] [[Category:American film actors]]
