{{Short description|Spanish Flamenco Singer}} {{Infobox person | honorific_prefix = | name = Rocío Márquez | image = Rio Loco 2015 Mercredi - Europe-7864.jpg | caption = Rocío Márquez at Rio Loco 2015 | birth_name = Rocío Márquez Limón | other_names = | birth_date = {{birth date|1985|9|29|df=yes}} | birth_place = [[Huelva]], [[Andalusia]], [[Kingdom of Spain]] | death_date = | death_place = | resting_place = | spouse = | partner = | children = | relatives = | occupation = {{hlist|Singer}} | years_active = 1994– | module = {{Infobox musical artist | embed = yes | genre = {{hlist|[[Flamenco music]], [[Nuevo flamenco]]}} | instrument = Vocals | label = {{hlist|[[Universal Music Group]]}} }} | notable_works = | awards = Coups de Coeur from the [[Académie Charles Cros]] (2013)
“Les Victoires du Jazz” for the Best World Music Album (2020)
Ruido Prize (Premio Ruido) for "Tercer Cielo" as best album (with Bronquio) (2022)
"Nana a medias" 2nd Carmen Awards, Best Original Song (2023)
"Fandango" 4th Carmen Awards, Best Original Song (2025) | website = }} '''Rocío Márquez Limón''' ([[Huelva]], September 29, 1985), known artistically as Rocío Márquez, is a Spanish [[flamenco]] singer, or [[cantaora]]. == Biography == From the age of nine, she took flamenco lessons at the Peña Flamenca in Huelva, made her first public appearance at that age. After beginning piano lessons, she appeared on the singing show 'Menudos Estrellas' on the Spanish television channel [[Antena 3 (Spanish TV channel)|Antena 3]] two years later, securing third place. A few months later, she won first prize in the 'Artistas Noveles' competition organized by the broadcaster [[Cadena COPE|COPE]]. During this period, she took singing lessons in Seville and appeared on several television programs, such as '{{ill|Esos locos bajitos|es}}' (1998–2005) and '{{ill|De buena mañana|es}}'.{{Cite web |last=RTVE |date=2022-02-15 |title=Roció Márquez, la cantaora que bajó a la mina para luchar con los mineros |url=https://www.rtve.es/play/noticias/20220215/rocio-marquez-minas-flamenco-canciones/2279661.shtml |access-date=2026-09-29 |website=RTVE.es |language=es}} In 2005, as a scholarship recipient of the Cristina Heeren Foundation, she received instruction from renowned flamenco artists, including {{ill|José de la Tomasa|es}} and {{ill|Paco Tarento|es}}.{{Cite web |title=Rocio Marquez {{!}} THEATREonline |url=https://www.theatreonline.com/Artiste/Rocio-Marquez/56519 |access-date=2026-09-29 |website=www.theatreonline.com}} In 2007, Rocío Márquez achieved notable success at various flamenco festivals, including those in Calasparra, Marchena, Mijas, and Jumilla. In 2008, she captivated audiences at the Las Minas Festival and International Competition in La Unión, where she received the prestigious "Lámpara Minera" award as well as four first-place prizes. In July 2010, she gave her first concert in France at the Les Suds festival in Arles, opening for Diego el Cigala.{{Cite news |title=Rocío Márquez, flamenco ensorcelé |url=https://next.liberation.fr/musique/2015/01/25/rocio-marquez-flamenco-ensorcele_1188432 |archive-url=http://web.archive.org/web/20210124225223/https://next.liberation.fr/musique/2015/01/25/rocio-marquez-flamenco-ensorcele_1188432 |archive-date=2021-01-24 |access-date=2026-09-29 |work=Libération.fr |language=fr}} Rocío Márquez earned her doctorate from the [[University of Seville]], with a dissertation focusing on "vocal technique in flamenco." She teaches in the inter-university master's program "Research and Analysis of Flamenco" and gives lectures on flamenco singing. {{Cite web |title=Rocío Márquez |url=https://www.cccb.org/ca/w/participants/rocio-marquez |access-date=2026-09-29 |website=CCCB |language=ca-ES}} She has performed on many stages in Spain, including the [[Teatro de la Zarzuela]], [[Teatro Real]], and [[National Auditorium of Music]] in Madrid; the Teatro Isabel la Católica in Granada; the [[Palau de la Música de València]]. Beyond Spain, she has performed at the [[Olympia (Paris)|Olympia in Paris]], the Auditorium in Brussels, and the [[Opernhaus Düsseldorf|Düsseldorf Opera House]]. Additionally, she has performed through the [[Instituto Cervantes]] in the United States, the Middle East, Argentina, Canada, and numerous European countries. In 2025, she launched her tour 'Himno Vertical', performing in Spain and Portugal.{{Cite web |date=2019-10-21 |title=Rocío Márquez |url=https://www.locomotivaazul.pt/en/artistas/rocio-marquez/ |access-date=2026-09-29 |website=Locomotiva Azul |language=en-GB}} == Awards == * 2008: ''Lámpara-minera'' Prize at the Cante de Las Minas Festival.{{Cite web |title=La cantaora onubense Rocío Márquez se lleva la 'Lámpara minera' en el Cante de Las Minas {{!}} elmundo.es |url=https://www.elmundo.es/elmundo/2008/08/17/cultura/1218960156.html |access-date=2026-09-29 |website=www.elmundo.es}} * 2013: Coups de Coeur de l’Académie de Charles Cros ([[Académie Charles Cros]]) (France, 2013). * 2016: Giraldillo for Dance{{Cite web |last=SGAE |first=Fundación |title=Entrega de los Giraldillos de la Bienal Internacional de Flamenco 2016 |url=https://fundacionsgae.org/actualidad/entrega-de-los-giraldillos-de-la-bienal-internacional-de-flamenco-2016/ |access-date=2026-09-29 |website=Fundación SGAE |language=es}} * 2019: Gold medal international competition Petenera{{Cite web |last=Ramos |first=Charo |date=2019-07-21 |title=Un viaje al centro de la petenera |url=https://www.diariodesevilla.es/ocio/Concurso-Cante-Peneteras-Paterna-Rivera_0_1374762746.html |access-date=2026-09-29 |website=Diario de Sevilla |language=es}} * 2020: “Les [[Victoires du Jazz]]” for the “Best World Music Album”{{Cite web |title=Une chanteuse espagnole primée aux “Victoires du Jazz”, une Première! |url=https://lepetitjournal.com/andalousie/une-chanteuse-espagnole-primee-aux-victoires-du-jazz-une-premiere-289659 |access-date=2026-09-29 |website=lepetitjournal.com |language=fr}} * 2022: Ruido Prize ([[Premio Ruido]]) for "Tercer Cielo" as best album (with Bronquio){{Cite web |last=Press |first=Europa |date=2023-02-10 |title='Tercer Cielo', de Rocío Márquez y Bronquio, Premio Ruido al Mejor Álbum Nacional de 2022 |url=https://www.europapress.es/navarra/noticia-tercer-cielo-rocio-marquez-bronquio-premio-ruido-mejor-album-nacional-2022-20230210100113.html |access-date=2026-09-29 |website=www.europapress.es |publisher=Europa Press}} * 2023: ''Nana a medias'' with Antonio Manuel and Javier Prieto [[2nd Carmen Awards]], Best Original Song * 2025: ''Fandango'' [[4th Carmen Awards]], Best Original Song == Discography == * 2009: ''Aquí y Ahora'' (DVD, El Séptimo Sello Records) * 2012: ''Claridad'' ([[Universal Music Group|Universal]]) * 2014: ''El niño'' consisting of songs by [[Pepe Marchena]] (Universal) * 2017: ''Firmamento''{{Cite news |date=April 27, 2017 |title=La cantaora Rocío Márquez crea un “Firmamento” nacido del alma |trans-title=Flamenco singer Rocío Márquez creates a "Firmamento" born of the soul |url=https://www.eldiario.es/cultura/cantaora-Rocio-Marquez-Firmamento-nacido_0_637637108.html |work=eldiario.es |language=Spanish}} (Universal) * 2018: ''Diálogos de nuevos y viejos sones'' (Alqhai&Alqhai) * 2019: ''Visto en'' El Jueves (Universal) * 2020: ''Omnia Vincit Amor'' (Digital EP) * 2022: ''Tercer cielo'' with 'Bronquio' (Universal) ==References== {{reflist}} {{Authority Control}} {{DEFAULTSORT:Márquez, Rocío}} [[Category:1985 births]] [[Category:Flamenco singers]] [[Category:Singers from Andalusia]] [[Category:Spanish-language singers]] [[Category:Spanish women singers]] [[Category:Living people]]

'''Daniele Canella''' (born 20 January 1991) is an Italian politician serving as president of the [[Province of Padua]] since 2026. He has also served as mayor of [[San Giorgio delle Pertiche]] since 2019.

==Life and career==
Canella was born in 1991 in [[Camposampiero]], in the [[province of Padua]].<ref name=interno/> He graduated from the Isaac Newton scientific high school in his hometown in 2009, and works as a self-employed insurance agent.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.comune.sangiorgiodellepertiche.pd.it/wp-content/uploads/2024/04/CV_sindaco_Redatto.pdf |title=CV Daniele Canella |work=Comune di San Giorgio delle Pertiche |access-date=29 September 2026}}</ref>

Canella was elected mayor of [[San Giorgio delle Pertiche]] in the [[2019 Italian local elections|2019 municipal elections]], receiving 61.9% of the vote.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://doc989.consiglioveneto.it/oe/resources/report_comunali2019_completo.pdf |title=San Giorgio delle Pertiche: risultati elezioni comunali 2019 |work=Consiglio regionale del Veneto |access-date=29 September 2026}}</ref> He was re-elected in 2024.<ref name=interno/>

A member of the [[Lega (political party)|Lega]], Canella served as vice president of the Province of Padua during the second half of [[Sergio Giordani]]'s term.<ref>{{Cite news |url=https://www.mattinopadova.it/cronaca/vicepresidente-provincia-padova-daniele-canella-dimissioni-ib0p1svk |title=Provincia, il vicepresidente Canella si congeda: "Ma è soltanto un arrivederci" |work=[[Il Mattino di Padova]] |first=Rocco |last=Currado |date=12 June 2026}}</ref> He was also a member of the national assembly of the [[Union of Italian Provinces]] (UPI) and of the executive board of UPI Veneto.<ref name=rai>{{cite news |url=https://www.rainews.it/tgr/veneto/video/2026/09/padova-insediato-daniele-canella-nuovo-presidente-della-provincia-ca5e59a9-266a-4487-8b33-6fe67daeb122.html |first=Lucia |last=Cappelletti |title=Padova, si è insediato Daniele Canella, nuovo presidente della Provincia |work=[[RAI|Rai News]] |date=16 September 2026 |access-date=29 September 2026}}</ref> In September 2026, Canella was elected [[president of the Province of Padua]].<ref>{{cite news |title=Provincia, Canella: "Costruirò la casa dei sindaci. Basta personalismi, penso al territorio" |url=https://www.mattinopadova.it/cronaca/provincia-padova-candidato-unico-canella-idee-programma-opo7k7oi |work=[[Il Mattino di Padova]] |date=27 August 2026 |first=Rocco |last=Currado |language=it |access-date=16 September 2026}}</ref><ref>{{cite news |url=https://www.mattinopadova.it/cronaca/daniele-canella-nuovo-presidente-provincia-padova-giordani-hshk41o8 |title=Daniele Canella è il nuovo presidente della Provincia di Padova: "Vittoria del territorio" |work=[[Il Mattino di Padova]] |date=15 September 2026 |first=Rocco |last=Currado |language=it |access-date=29 September 2026}}</ref> At 35, he became the youngest president in the history of the Province of Padua and the youngest provincial president in Italy.<ref name=rai/><ref>{{Cite news |url=https://www.difesapopolo.it/provincia-largo-al-giovane-daniele-canella-e-il-nuovo-presidente-della-provincia-di-padova/ |title=Provincia, largo al giovane. Daniele Canella è il nuovo presidente della Provincia di Padova |first=Claudio |last=Baccarin |work=La Difesa del Popolo |date=27 September 2026}}</ref>

'''Maho Ono''' ({{langx|ja|尾野 真歩}}; born 9 February 1999) is a Japanese [[karate]]ka who competes in [[Karate kata|women's individual kata]].<ref name="JKF">{{Cite web
|title=尾野 真歩
|url=https://www.jkf.ne.jp/national_member/ono_maho
|website=Japan Karate Federation
|access-date=3 October 2026
}}</ref> She won the gold medal in the women's individual kata event at the [[2026 Asian Games]] in Aichi and Nagoya, Japan.<ref name="JOC">{{Cite web
|title=尾野 真歩
|url=https://joc.or.jp/athletes/onomaho/index.html
|website=[[Japanese Olympic Committee]]
|access-date=3 October 2026
}}</ref> She also won the gold medal at the [[2026 Asian Karate Championships]] in Bali, Indonesia, and the silver medal at the [[2025 World Karate Championships]] in Cairo, Egypt.<ref name="JKF"/><ref name="WKF2025">{{Cite web
|title=Karate World Championships - Individual World Championships - Cairo 2025
|url=https://www.karatedo.co.jp/jkn_wp/wp-content/uploads/2025/12/Resultbook.pdf
|website=Japan Karate Federation
|access-date=3 October 2026
}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=International |first=JKFan NEWS |date=2026-09-20 |title=【速報 アジア大会】尾野真歩が金メダル！グレースに５ー０完勝で優勝！ 愛知 アジア大会１日目 |url=https://www.karatedo.co.jp/news/topics/20260920/71013 |access-date=2026-10-03 |website=JKFan NEWS International (空手ワールド) |language=ja}}</ref>

==Career==

Ono began practising karate at the age of five. She attended Nihon University Tsurugaoka High School before studying at [[Keio University]], where she was a member of the university karate club. She later joined [[Kikkoman]] and continued competing internationally in women's individual kata.<ref name="JKF"/><ref name="Tokyo">{{Cite web
|title=National Sports and All-Athlete Sports Support Site
|url=https://en.sports-tokyo-info.metro.tokyo.lg.jp/kokusupo-zensupo-tokyo-athlete/interview/896/
|website=Sports Tokyo Information
|access-date=3 October 2026
}}</ref>

In 2022, Ono finished third at the All Japan Karate Championships. The following year, she won bronze medals at the [[Karate1 Premier League]] events in Dublin and Cairo and finished fifth in Rabat.<ref name="Tokyo2">{{Cite web
|title=Tokyo-raised athlete support project
|url=https://en.sports-tokyo-info.metro.tokyo.lg.jp/sodachi/athlete/1292.html
|website=Sports Tokyo Information
|access-date=3 October 2026
}}</ref>

Ono had a breakthrough season in 2024. She won the women's individual kata events at the [[2024 Karate1 Premier League]] tournaments in Paris and Casablanca. Her results across the season also earned her the Premier League Grand Winner title in women's kata.<ref name="JKF"/><ref name="Tokyo2"/>

In May 2025, Ono won the silver medal in women's individual kata at the [[2025 Asian Karate Championships]] in Tashkent, Uzbekistan.<ref name="WKFrank">{{Cite web
|title=WKF Ranking - Profile: Maho Ono
|url=https://setopen.sportdata.org/wkfranking/ranking_main_detail.php?category=490&wkfcode=JPN2451
|website=[[World Karate Federation]]
|access-date=3 October 2026
}}</ref> Later that year, she won the silver medal at the [[2025 World Games]] in Chengdu, China, finishing behind Hong Kong's [[Grace Lau]]. At the [[2025 World Karate Championships]] in Cairo, she again won silver in individual kata, finishing second behind Grace Lau.<ref name="WKF2025"/><ref>{{Cite web |last=JKFエディター |date=2025-12-02 |title=第27回世界選手権（個人戦）・第６回世界パラ選手権で、日本選手が５つのメダル獲得 {{!}} 公益財団法人 全日本空手道連盟 |url=https://www.jkf.ne.jp/info/competition/20251202/34533 |access-date=2026-10-03 |language=ja}}</ref>

In June 2026, Ono won the women's individual kata title at the [[2026 Asian Karate Championships]] in Bali, Indonesia. Her victory made her the first Asian champion in women's individual kata from Keio University's karate club.<ref name="Keio">{{Cite web
|title=空手部 / アジアシニア空手道選手権大会・女子個人形で、尾野真歩君が優勝
|url=https://www.uaa.keio.ac.jp/topics/202606191303.html
|website=Keio University Athletics Association
|date=19 June 2026
|access-date=3 October 2026
}}</ref>

At the [[2026 Asian Games]] in Aichi and Nagoya, Ono won the gold medal in the women's individual kata event. She defeated Hong Kong's Grace Lau in the final, becoming the ninth consecutive Japanese winner of the women's individual kata title at the Asian Games.<ref name="JOC"/><ref name="AsianGames2026">{{Cite web
|title=Asian Games 2026 Karate Results
|url=https://www.the-karatedojo.com/calendar/asian-games-karate-2026/
|website=The Karate Dojo
|access-date=3 October 2026
}}</ref>

=== Frist years and education ===
The granddaughter of [[Francisca Motta]] and daughter of {{Interlanguage link|Nabor Wanderley|lt=Nabor Wanderley|pt|Nabor Wanderley}}, Olivia was born on 15 April 1991 in [[João Pessoa, Paraíba|João Pessoa]], the capital of [[Paraíba]].<ref name="Website-1" /><ref>{{Cite web |date=October 14, 2026 |title=Eleições 2026: Ficha de Olívia Motta (REPUBLICANOS) {{!}} Folha |url=https://www1.folha.uol.com.br/poder/eleicoes/candidatos/2026/pb/deputado-estadual/olivia-motta-150002544186.shtml |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20261011133454/https://www1.folha.uol.com.br/poder/eleicoes/candidatos/2026/pb/deputado-estadual/olivia-motta-150002544186.shtml |archive-date=October 11, 2026 |access-date=October 14, 2026 |website=[[Folha de S.Paulo]] |language=pt-BR}}</ref> She studied [[medicine]] at the Nova Esperança School of Nursing (FACENE), where she later specialized in [[radiology]].<ref>{{cite web|access-date=October 7, 2026 |archive-date=October 14, 2026 |archive-url=https://megalodon.jp/2026-1007-2328-10/lattes.cnpq.br/2426625102257633 |title=Olivia Motta Wanderley da Nóbrega |url=http://buscatextual.cnpq.br/buscatextual/visualizacv.do?metodo=apresentar&id=K8161017Z4 |url-status=live |website=[[National Council for Scientific and Technological Development]]}}<!-- auto-translated from Portuguese by Module:CS1 translator --></ref>
